text.en: A switch receives a frame on interface Fa0/4. Which information does the switch use to build its MAC address table?
text.hi: Ek switch interface Fa0/4 par ek frame receive karta hai. Switch apni MAC address table banane ke liye kaunsi information use karta hai?

explanation.en: Switches learn passively: for every frame received, the switch records the frame's SOURCE MAC address against the ingress interface (and VLAN). The destination MAC is only used afterward to look up where to forward the frame.
explanation.hi: Switches passively seekhte hain: har receive hue frame ke liye switch frame ka SOURCE MAC address ingress interface (aur VLAN) ke against record karta hai. Destination MAC sirf baad mein yeh dekhne ke liye use hota hai ki frame kahan forward karna hai.

options.en: The destination MAC address of the frame
options.hi: Frame ka destination MAC address

options.en: The source MAC address of the frame and the interface it arrived on
options.hi: Frame ka source MAC address aur woh interface jis par woh aaya

options.en: The source IP address of the packet inside the frame
options.hi: Frame ke andar packet ka source IP address

options.en: An ARP request the switch sends to the connected host
options.hi: Ek ARP request jo switch connected host ko bhejta hai

whyWrong.en: The destination MAC is used to make the forwarding decision, not to learn entries.
whyWrong.hi: Destination MAC forwarding decision lene ke liye use hota hai, entries seekhne ke liye nahi.

whyWrong.en: A Layer 2 switch does not inspect IP addresses to populate the MAC (CAM) table.
whyWrong.hi: Layer 2 switch MAC (CAM) table bharne ke liye IP addresses inspect nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: Switches learn from frames they receive; they do not send ARP requests to discover hosts — ARP is a host/router function.
whyWrong.hi: Switches receive hue frames se seekhte hain; woh hosts discover karne ke liye ARP requests nahi bhejte — ARP host/router ka function hai.

text.en: SW1 receives a unicast frame whose destination MAC address is not in its MAC address table. What does the switch do with the frame?
text.hi: SW1 ek unicast frame receive karta hai jiska destination MAC address uski MAC address table mein nahi hai. Switch us frame ka kya karta hai?

explanation.en: An unknown unicast is flooded out every port in the same VLAN except the ingress port. When the destination replies, the switch learns its MAC from that reply's source address and future frames are forwarded out only the correct port.
explanation.hi: Unknown unicast ko same VLAN ke har port par flood kiya jaata hai, ingress port ko chhod kar. Jab destination reply karta hai, switch us reply ke source address se uska MAC seekh leta hai aur aage ke frames sirf sahi port par forward hote hain.

options.en: Drops the frame until the destination is learned
options.hi: Destination seekhne tak frame drop kar deta hai

options.en: Floods it out all ports in the same VLAN except the port it arrived on
options.hi: Use same VLAN ke saare ports par flood karta hai, sirf us port ko chhod kar jis par woh aaya

options.en: Sends it to the CPU so the switch can generate an ARP request
options.hi: Use CPU ko bhejta hai taaki switch ARP request generate kar sake

options.en: Forwards it only out trunk ports
options.hi: Use sirf trunk ports par forward karta hai

whyWrong.en: Dropping would break communication with hosts the switch has not learned yet; flooding guarantees delivery.
whyWrong.hi: Drop karne se un hosts ke saath communication toot jaata jinhe switch ne abhi tak seekha nahi; flooding delivery guarantee karti hai.

whyWrong.en: The data plane floods the frame; the switch does not ARP on behalf of hosts.
whyWrong.hi: Data plane frame ko flood karta hai; switch hosts ki taraf se ARP nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: Flooding covers ALL ports in the VLAN (access and trunk), not just trunks.
whyWrong.hi: Flooding VLAN ke SAARE ports (access aur trunk) par hoti hai, sirf trunks par nahi.

text.en: Which switching method starts forwarding a frame as soon as the destination MAC address (the first 6 bytes after the preamble) has been read, without waiting for the rest of the frame?
text.hi: Kaunsa switching method destination MAC address (preamble ke baad pehle 6 bytes) padhte hi frame forward karna shuru kar deta hai, baaki frame ka wait kiye bina?

explanation.en: Cut-through switching begins forwarding immediately after reading the destination MAC, minimizing latency. The trade-off is that it cannot check the FCS first, so corrupted frames may be propagated.
explanation.hi: Cut-through switching destination MAC padhne ke turant baad forwarding shuru kar deta hai, jisse latency minimum rehti hai. Iski keemat yeh hai ki yeh pehle FCS check nahi kar sakta, isliye corrupted frames aage ja sakte hain.

options.en: Store-and-forward
options.hi: Store-and-forward

options.en: Fragment-free
options.hi: Fragment-free

options.en: Cut-through
options.hi: Cut-through

options.en: Adaptive load balancing
options.hi: Adaptive load balancing

whyWrong.en: Store-and-forward buffers the ENTIRE frame and verifies the FCS/CRC before forwarding.
whyWrong.hi: Store-and-forward POORE frame ko buffer karta hai aur forward karne se pehle FCS/CRC verify karta hai.

whyWrong.en: Fragment-free waits for the first 64 bytes (the collision window) before forwarding — a compromise, not immediate forwarding.
whyWrong.hi: Fragment-free forward karne se pehle pehle 64 bytes (collision window) ka wait karta hai — yeh ek compromise hai, turant forwarding nahi.

whyWrong.en: Adaptive load balancing is a NIC-teaming technique, not a switch forwarding method.
whyWrong.hi: Adaptive load balancing ek NIC-teaming technique hai, switch forwarding method nahi.

text.en:
Examine this output:

SW1# show mac address-table dynamic
          Mac Address Table
-------------------------------------------
Vlan    Mac Address       Type        Ports
----    -----------       --------    -----
  10    0050.7966.6a01    DYNAMIC     Fa0/1
  10    0050.7966.6a02    DYNAMIC     Fa0/1
  10    0050.7966.6a03    DYNAMIC     Fa0/3

A frame arrives on Fa0/1 in VLAN 10 with source MAC 0050.7966.6a01 and destination MAC 0050.7966.6a02. What does SW1 do?
text.hi:
Yeh output dekho:

SW1# show mac address-table dynamic
          Mac Address Table
-------------------------------------------
Vlan    Mac Address       Type        Ports
----    -----------       --------    -----
  10    0050.7966.6a01    DYNAMIC     Fa0/1
  10    0050.7966.6a02    DYNAMIC     Fa0/1
  10    0050.7966.6a03    DYNAMIC     Fa0/3

Ek frame VLAN 10 mein Fa0/1 par aata hai jiska source MAC 0050.7966.6a01 aur destination MAC 0050.7966.6a02 hai. SW1 kya karta hai?

explanation.en: Both MACs live on Fa0/1 (for example two devices behind a small hub or an IP phone). The frame already reached that segment, and a switch never forwards a frame out its ingress port. Since the destination is known and maps to the receiving port, the switch filters (drops) the frame.
explanation.hi: Dono MACs Fa0/1 par hain (jaise ek chhote hub ke peeche do devices ya ek IP phone). Frame pehle hi us segment tak pahunch chuka hai, aur switch kabhi frame ko uske ingress port par wapas forward nahi karta. Kyunki destination known hai aur receiving port par hi map hota hai, switch frame ko filter (drop) kar deta hai.

options.en: Floods the frame out all VLAN 10 ports
options.hi: Frame ko VLAN 10 ke saare ports par flood karta hai

options.en: Forwards the frame out Fa0/3
options.hi: Frame ko Fa0/3 par forward karta hai

options.en: Discards (filters) the frame because the destination is reachable via the same port it arrived on
options.hi: Frame ko discard (filter) kar deta hai kyunki destination usi port se reachable hai jis par frame aaya

options.en: Forwards the frame back out Fa0/1 toward the destination
options.hi: Frame ko destination ki taraf wapas Fa0/1 par forward karta hai

whyWrong.en: Flooding happens only for unknown unicasts, broadcasts, and some multicasts — this destination IS in the table.
whyWrong.hi: Flooding sirf unknown unicasts, broadcasts aur kuch multicasts ke liye hoti hai — yeh destination table mein HAI.

whyWrong.en: Fa0/3 holds a different MAC (…6a03); the table maps the destination to Fa0/1.
whyWrong.hi: Fa0/3 par ek alag MAC (…6a03) hai; table destination ko Fa0/1 par map karti hai.

whyWrong.en: A switch never sends a frame back out the interface it arrived on.
whyWrong.hi: Switch kabhi frame ko usi interface par wapas nahi bhejta jis par woh aaya tha.

text.en: Which three statements about MAC address table operation on a Catalyst switch are true? (Choose three.)
text.hi: Catalyst switch par MAC address table operation ke baare mein kaunse teen statements sahi hain? (Teen chuno.)

explanation.en: Dynamic entries age out after 300 seconds by default, learning is based on source MAC + ingress port, and when a host moves (or a topology change re-routes its traffic) the switch updates the entry to the most recent port. Broadcasts are flooded but never learned, and unknown unicasts are flooded, not dropped.
explanation.hi: Dynamic entries default mein 300 seconds baad age out ho jaati hain, learning source MAC + ingress port par based hai, aur jab koi host move karta hai (ya topology change uska traffic re-route karta hai) toh switch entry ko sabse recent port par update kar deta hai. Broadcasts flood hote hain lekin kabhi learn nahi hote, aur unknown unicasts flood hote hain, drop nahi.

options.en: Dynamic entries age out after 300 seconds of inactivity by default
options.hi: Dynamic entries default mein 300 seconds inactivity ke baad age out ho jaati hain

options.en: The switch records the source MAC and ingress port of each frame it receives
options.hi: Switch har receive hue frame ka source MAC aur ingress port record karta hai

options.en: Broadcast frames cause the switch to learn an entry for ffff.ffff.ffff
options.hi: Broadcast frames ki wajah se switch ffff.ffff.ffff ki entry seekh leta hai

options.en: If a known MAC is seen arriving on a different port, the entry is updated to the new port
options.hi: Agar ek known MAC alag port par aata dikhe, toh entry naye port par update ho jaati hai

options.en: Frames to an unknown unicast destination are dropped until the destination is learned
options.hi: Unknown unicast destination wale frames destination seekhne tak drop hote hain

whyWrong.en: ffff.ffff.ffff is never a valid SOURCE address, so it is never learned; broadcast frames are simply flooded.
whyWrong.hi: ffff.ffff.ffff kabhi valid SOURCE address nahi hota, isliye yeh kabhi learn nahi hota; broadcast frames bas flood ho jaate hain.

whyWrong.en: Unknown unicast frames are flooded within the VLAN so the destination can still receive them.
whyWrong.hi: Unknown unicast frames VLAN ke andar flood hote hain taaki destination unhe phir bhi receive kar sake.

text.en: An administrator plans to create VLAN 2500 on a Catalyst switch. Which statement about this VLAN ID is true?
text.hi: Ek administrator Catalyst switch par VLAN 2500 banana chahta hai. Is VLAN ID ke baare mein kaunsa statement sahi hai?

explanation.en: Normal-range VLANs are 1–1005 (with 1002–1005 reserved for legacy media). Extended-range VLANs are 1006–4094, so VLAN 2500 falls in the extended range. On VTP version 1 and 2, extended VLANs can only be created in VTP transparent mode.
explanation.hi: Normal-range VLANs 1–1005 hain (jismein 1002–1005 legacy media ke liye reserved hain). Extended-range VLANs 1006–4094 hain, isliye VLAN 2500 extended range mein aata hai. VTP version 1 aur 2 par extended VLANs sirf VTP transparent mode mein banaye ja sakte hain.

options.en: It is a normal-range VLAN like any other
options.hi: Yeh baaki sab ki tarah ek normal-range VLAN hai

options.en: It is an extended-range VLAN, because the extended range covers 1006 through 4094
options.hi: Yeh extended-range VLAN hai, kyunki extended range 1006 se 4094 tak hai

options.en: It is invalid — VLAN IDs stop at 1005
options.hi: Yeh invalid hai — VLAN IDs 1005 par khatam ho jaate hain

options.en: It is reserved for FDDI and Token Ring
options.hi: Yeh FDDI aur Token Ring ke liye reserved hai

whyWrong.en: The normal range ends at 1005; 2500 is beyond it.
whyWrong.hi: Normal range 1005 par khatam hoti hai; 2500 usse aage hai.

whyWrong.en: 802.1Q supports VLAN IDs up to 4094, so 2500 is valid.
whyWrong.hi: 802.1Q 4094 tak VLAN IDs support karta hai, isliye 2500 valid hai.

whyWrong.en: VLANs 1002–1005 are the legacy FDDI/Token Ring VLANs, not 2500.
whyWrong.hi: VLANs 1002–1005 legacy FDDI/Token Ring VLANs hain, 2500 nahi.

text.en: Which configuration correctly makes interface Fa0/8 an access port in VLAN 20?
text.hi: Kaunsi configuration interface Fa0/8 ko sahi tareeke se VLAN 20 mein access port banati hai?

explanation.en: An access port carries one data VLAN. The pair of interface commands is: switchport mode access (force access mode, disabling trunk negotiation) and switchport access vlan 20 (assign the VLAN). If VLAN 20 does not exist yet, the switch creates it automatically.
explanation.hi: Access port ek data VLAN carry karta hai. Interface commands ki jodi hai: switchport mode access (access mode force karo, trunk negotiation disable karke) aur switchport access vlan 20 (VLAN assign karo). Agar VLAN 20 abhi exist nahi karta, toh switch use automatically bana deta hai.

options.en: switchport mode access, then switchport access vlan 20
options.hi: switchport mode access, phir switchport access vlan 20

options.en: switchport mode trunk, then switchport trunk vlan 20
options.hi: switchport mode trunk, phir switchport trunk vlan 20

options.en: switchport vlan 20 access
options.hi: switchport vlan 20 access

options.en: vlan 20 mode access
options.hi: vlan 20 mode access

whyWrong.en: Trunk mode carries many VLANs with 802.1Q tags — the opposite of a single-VLAN access port, and 'switchport trunk vlan' is not valid syntax.
whyWrong.hi: Trunk mode 802.1Q tags ke saath kai VLANs carry karta hai — single-VLAN access port ka ulta, aur 'switchport trunk vlan' valid syntax nahi hai.

whyWrong.en: 'switchport vlan 20 access' is not a valid IOS command.
whyWrong.hi: 'switchport vlan 20 access' valid IOS command nahi hai.

whyWrong.en: 'vlan 20 mode access' is not valid — vlan 20 in global config only creates the VLAN.
whyWrong.hi: 'vlan 20 mode access' valid nahi hai — global config mein vlan 20 sirf VLAN banata hai.

text.en:
PC-A on Fa0/1 and PC-B on Fa0/3 are both supposed to be in the SALES VLAN and cannot ping each other. Both links show connected.

SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -----------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/2, Fa0/3, Fa0/4
10   SALES                            active    Fa0/1
20   ENGINEERING                      active

What is the problem?
text.hi:
Fa0/1 par PC-A aur Fa0/3 par PC-B dono SALES VLAN mein hone chahiye aur ek doosre ko ping nahi kar pa rahe. Dono links connected dikh rahe hain.

SW1# show vlan brief
VLAN Name                             Status    Ports
---- -------------------------------- --------- -----------------------
1    default                          active    Fa0/2, Fa0/3, Fa0/4
10   SALES                            active    Fa0/1
20   ENGINEERING                      active

Problem kya hai?

explanation.en: The output shows Fa0/3 listed under VLAN 1 (default), not VLAN 10. Ports keep their default VLAN 1 membership until switchport access vlan 10 is applied. Because the PCs are in different VLANs, they are in separate broadcast domains and cannot reach each other at Layer 2.
explanation.hi: Output mein Fa0/3 VLAN 1 (default) ke neeche list hai, VLAN 10 ke neeche nahi. Ports tab tak apni default VLAN 1 membership rakhte hain jab tak switchport access vlan 10 apply na kiya jaaye. Kyunki PCs alag VLANs mein hain, woh alag broadcast domains mein hain aur Layer 2 par ek doosre tak nahi pahunch sakte.

options.en: Fa0/3 was never assigned to VLAN 10, so PC-B is still in VLAN 1
options.hi: Fa0/3 ko kabhi VLAN 10 assign nahi kiya gaya, isliye PC-B abhi bhi VLAN 1 mein hai

options.en: VLAN 10 is not active on the switch
options.hi: Switch par VLAN 10 active nahi hai

options.en: Fa0/1 is configured as a trunk
options.hi: Fa0/1 trunk ki tarah configured hai

options.en: The ENGINEERING VLAN is overlapping with SALES
options.hi: ENGINEERING VLAN SALES ke saath overlap kar raha hai

whyWrong.en: The Status column shows VLAN 10 as active.
whyWrong.hi: Status column VLAN 10 ko active dikhata hai.

whyWrong.en: A trunk port would not appear in the show vlan brief port list at all — Fa0/1 appears under VLAN 10, so it is an access port.
whyWrong.hi: Trunk port show vlan brief ki port list mein dikhta hi nahi — Fa0/1 VLAN 10 ke neeche dikh raha hai, isliye yeh access port hai.

whyWrong.en: VLAN 20 has no ports assigned and is unrelated to the problem.
whyWrong.hi: VLAN 20 par koi port assigned nahi hai aur iska problem se koi lena dena nahi.

text.en: Which two statements about VLAN ranges and default VLANs on a Catalyst switch are accurate? (Choose two.)
text.hi: Catalyst switch par VLAN ranges aur default VLANs ke baare mein kaunse do statements sahi hain? (Do chuno.)

explanation.en: VLAN 1 plus the reserved legacy VLANs 1002-1005 always exist and cannot be removed. Under VTP v1/v2 the switch must be in transparent mode to configure extended-range VLANs (VTP v3 can propagate them). Pruning VLAN 1 from a trunk removes user data but control protocols such as CDP, DTP, VTP, and PAgP are still sent.
explanation.hi: VLAN 1 aur reserved legacy VLANs 1002-1005 hamesha exist karte hain aur hataye nahi ja sakte. VTP v1/v2 mein extended-range VLANs configure karne ke liye switch ka transparent mode mein hona zaroori hai (VTP v3 unhe propagate kar sakta hai). Trunk se VLAN 1 prune karne par user data hat jaata hai lekin CDP, DTP, VTP aur PAgP jaise control protocols phir bhi bheje jaate hain.

options.en: VLAN 1 and VLANs 1002-1005 exist by default and cannot be deleted
options.hi: VLAN 1 aur VLANs 1002-1005 default mein exist karte hain aur delete nahi kiye ja sakte

options.en: With VTP version 1 or 2, extended-range VLANs (1006-4094) can be created only in VTP transparent mode
options.hi: VTP version 1 ya 2 ke saath extended-range VLANs (1006-4094) sirf VTP transparent mode mein banaye ja sakte hain

options.en: The normal VLAN range covers IDs 1 through 4094
options.hi: Normal VLAN range IDs 1 se 4094 tak cover karti hai

options.en: Removing VLAN 1 from a trunk's allowed list also blocks CDP, DTP, and other control protocols
options.hi: Trunk ki allowed list se VLAN 1 hatane par CDP, DTP aur doosre control protocols bhi block ho jaate hain

options.en: The extended range covers IDs 1002 through 4094
options.hi: Extended range IDs 1002 se 4094 tak cover karti hai

whyWrong.en: The normal range is 1-1005; 1006-4094 is the extended range.
whyWrong.hi: Normal range 1-1005 hai; 1006-4094 extended range hai.

whyWrong.en: Control-plane protocols like CDP and DTP continue to be sent on the trunk even when VLAN 1 is removed from the allowed list.
whyWrong.hi: CDP aur DTP jaise control-plane protocols trunk par bheje jaate rehte hain, chahe VLAN 1 allowed list se hata diya gaya ho.

whyWrong.en: The extended range starts at 1006; 1002-1005 are reserved normal-range VLANs.
whyWrong.hi: Extended range 1006 se shuru hoti hai; 1002-1005 reserved normal-range VLANs hain.

text.en: Type the command that displays a one-line-per-VLAN summary showing each VLAN's ID, name, status, and assigned access ports.
text.hi: Woh command type karo jo har VLAN ki ek-line summary dikhata hai jismein har VLAN ka ID, name, status aur assigned access ports hon.

explanation.en: show vlan brief lists every VLAN with its status and the access ports assigned to it. Trunk ports do not appear in this listing, which itself is a useful troubleshooting clue.
explanation.hi: show vlan brief har VLAN ko uske status aur usse assigned access ports ke saath list karta hai. Trunk ports is listing mein nahi dikhte, jo khud troubleshooting ka ek useful clue hai.

text.en: How does an 802.1Q trunk carry traffic that belongs to the native VLAN?
text.hi: 802.1Q trunk native VLAN ka traffic kaise carry karta hai?

explanation.en: 802.1Q defines one native VLAN per trunk whose frames cross the link without a tag. Any untagged frame received on the trunk is assumed to belong to the native VLAN — which is why the native VLAN must match on both ends.
explanation.hi: 802.1Q har trunk par ek native VLAN define karta hai jiske frames bina tag ke link cross karte hain. Trunk par receive hua koi bhi untagged frame native VLAN ka maana jaata hai — isi wajah se native VLAN dono ends par match hona chahiye.

options.en: It is sent untagged
options.hi: Yeh untagged bheja jaata hai

options.en: It is tagged with the native VLAN ID
options.hi: Yeh native VLAN ID se tag kiya jaata hai

options.en: It is encapsulated with an additional ISL header
options.hi: Yeh ek extra ISL header ke saath encapsulate hota hai

options.en: It is always carried in VLAN 1 with a tag
options.hi: Yeh hamesha tag ke saath VLAN 1 mein carry hota hai

whyWrong.en: Native VLAN frames are the one exception to tagging on an 802.1Q trunk.
whyWrong.hi: 802.1Q trunk par tagging ka ek hi exception native VLAN frames hain.

whyWrong.en: ISL is a legacy Cisco encapsulation that tagged every frame; it is not used with 802.1Q.
whyWrong.hi: ISL ek legacy Cisco encapsulation hai jo har frame ko tag karta tha; 802.1Q ke saath yeh use nahi hota.

whyWrong.en: The native VLAN defaults to VLAN 1 but can be changed, and its traffic is untagged, not tagged.
whyWrong.hi: Native VLAN default mein VLAN 1 hota hai lekin badla ja sakta hai, aur iska traffic untagged hota hai, tagged nahi.

text.en:
Users in VLAN 20 on SW1 cannot reach VLAN 20 servers behind SW2. VLANs 10 and 30 work fine across the same link.

SW1# show interfaces trunk
Port        Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1       on           802.1q         trunking      1

Port        Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1       1,10,30

Port        Vlans allowed and active in management domain
Gi0/1       1,10,30

Why is VLAN 20 traffic failing?
text.hi:
SW1 par VLAN 20 ke users SW2 ke peeche VLAN 20 servers tak nahi pahunch pa rahe. Usi link par VLANs 10 aur 30 theek chal rahe hain.

SW1# show interfaces trunk
Port        Mode         Encapsulation  Status        Native vlan
Gi0/1       on           802.1q         trunking      1

Port        Vlans allowed on trunk
Gi0/1       1,10,30

Port        Vlans allowed and active in management domain
Gi0/1       1,10,30

VLAN 20 traffic fail kyun ho raha hai?

explanation.en: The allowed list shows only 1,10,30 — VLAN 20 was pruned from the trunk, so its frames never cross the link. Fix it with: switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20 (the add keyword preserves the existing list).
explanation.hi: Allowed list sirf 1,10,30 dikhati hai — VLAN 20 trunk se prune ho gaya hai, isliye uske frames kabhi link cross nahi karte. Ise is command se fix karo: switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20 (add keyword existing list ko bachaye rakhta hai).

options.en: VLAN 20 is not in the trunk's allowed VLAN list
options.hi: VLAN 20 trunk ki allowed VLAN list mein nahi hai

options.en: The native VLAN must be changed to 20
options.hi: Native VLAN ko 20 mein badalna padega

options.en: VLAN 20 is being blocked by spanning tree
options.hi: VLAN 20 ko spanning tree block kar raha hai

options.en: The trunk negotiated the wrong encapsulation
options.hi: Trunk ne galat encapsulation negotiate kiya

whyWrong.en: The native VLAN only controls which VLAN travels untagged; it does not need to be 20 for tagged VLAN 20 traffic to pass.
whyWrong.hi: Native VLAN sirf yeh control karta hai ki kaunsa VLAN untagged jaayega; tagged VLAN 20 traffic pass hone ke liye ise 20 hone ki zaroorat nahi.

whyWrong.en: STP blocks entire ports per VLAN; here VLAN 20 is simply absent from the allowed list, which is shown directly in the output.
whyWrong.hi: STP har VLAN ke liye poore ports block karta hai; yahan VLAN 20 bas allowed list se gayab hai, jo output mein seedha dikh raha hai.

whyWrong.en: Status shows 802.1q and trunking — encapsulation is fine, since VLANs 10 and 30 work.
whyWrong.hi: Status 802.1q aur trunking dikha raha hai — encapsulation theek hai, kyunki VLANs 10 aur 30 kaam kar rahe hain.

text.en: Trunk Gi0/1 currently allows VLANs 10, 20, and 30. An administrator intends to add VLAN 40 and types: switchport trunk allowed vlan 40. What is the result?
text.hi: Trunk Gi0/1 abhi VLANs 10, 20 aur 30 allow karta hai. Ek administrator VLAN 40 add karna chahta hai aur type karta hai: switchport trunk allowed vlan 40. Result kya hoga?

explanation.en: Without the add keyword, switchport trunk allowed vlan REPLACES the entire list. The trunk now carries only VLAN 40, causing an instant outage for VLANs 10, 20, and 30. The correct command was: switchport trunk allowed vlan add 40. This is a classic real-world (and exam) trap.
explanation.hi: add keyword ke bina switchport trunk allowed vlan poori list ko REPLACE kar deta hai. Trunk ab sirf VLAN 40 carry karta hai, jisse VLANs 10, 20 aur 30 ke liye turant outage ho jaata hai. Sahi command thi: switchport trunk allowed vlan add 40. Yeh real world (aur exam) ka classic trap hai.

options.en: VLAN 40 is added and VLANs 10, 20, and 30 keep working
options.hi: VLAN 40 add ho jaata hai aur VLANs 10, 20 aur 30 kaam karte rehte hain

options.en: Only VLAN 40 is now allowed — traffic for VLANs 10, 20, and 30 stops crossing the trunk
options.hi: Ab sirf VLAN 40 allowed hai — VLANs 10, 20 aur 30 ka traffic trunk cross karna band kar deta hai

options.en: The command is rejected because the add keyword is mandatory
options.hi: Command reject ho jaata hai kyunki add keyword mandatory hai

options.en: All VLANs become allowed because the list is reset to the default
options.hi: Saare VLANs allowed ho jaate hain kyunki list default par reset ho jaati hai

whyWrong.en: That would be the effect of using the add keyword, which was omitted.
whyWrong.hi: Yeh add keyword use karne ka effect hota, jo chhoot gaya tha.

whyWrong.en: IOS accepts the command; add is optional syntax that changes the behavior, not a required keyword.
whyWrong.hi: IOS command accept kar leta hai; add optional syntax hai jo behavior badalta hai, required keyword nahi.

whyWrong.en: The default allow-all list is restored with 'switchport trunk allowed vlan all' or 'no switchport trunk allowed vlan' — not by naming a single VLAN.
whyWrong.hi: Default allow-all list 'switchport trunk allowed vlan all' ya 'no switchport trunk allowed vlan' se restore hoti hai — ek single VLAN ka naam lene se nahi.

text.en: Match each switchport mode to its DTP behavior.
text.hi: Har switchport mode ko uske DTP behavior se match karo.

explanation.en: Desirable initiates negotiation; auto only responds, so auto + auto stays an access link. Mode trunk forces trunking but keeps sending DTP (pair it with nonegotiate to silence DTP). Mode access never trunks. Nonegotiate disables DTP and requires the mode to be statically set.
explanation.hi: Desirable negotiation initiate karta hai; auto sirf respond karta hai, isliye auto + auto access link hi rehta hai. Mode trunk trunking force karta hai lekin DTP bhejta rehta hai (DTP chup karane ke liye ise nonegotiate ke saath use karo). Mode access kabhi trunk nahi banta. Nonegotiate DTP disable karta hai aur mode ko statically set karna zaroori bana deta hai.

right.en: Actively sends DTP frames to negotiate a trunk
right.hi: Trunk negotiate karne ke liye actively DTP frames bhejta hai

right.en: Becomes a trunk only if the neighbor initiates negotiation
right.hi: Trunk sirf tab banta hai jab neighbor negotiation initiate kare

right.en: Permanent trunk that still sends DTP frames
right.hi: Permanent trunk jo phir bhi DTP frames bhejta hai

right.en: Permanent non-trunk regardless of what the neighbor sends
right.hi: Permanent non-trunk, chahe neighbor kuch bhi bheje

right.en: Stops DTP frames from being sent on the port
right.hi: Port par DTP frames bhejna band kar deta hai

text.en: Type the command that lists the interfaces currently trunking, along with each trunk's mode, encapsulation, native VLAN, and allowed VLANs.
text.hi: Woh command type karo jo abhi trunking kar rahe interfaces ko list karta hai, saath mein har trunk ka mode, encapsulation, native VLAN aur allowed VLANs.

explanation.en: show interfaces trunk is the first command for any trunking problem: it confirms whether the port is actually trunking, the native VLAN (mismatches cause leakage), and which VLANs are allowed, active, and unpruned.
explanation.hi: show interfaces trunk kisi bhi trunking problem ke liye pehla command hai: yeh confirm karta hai ki port asal mein trunking kar raha hai ya nahi, native VLAN kya hai (mismatch se leakage hota hai), aur kaunse VLANs allowed, active aur unpruned hain.

text.en: Hosts in VLAN 10 (10.1.10.0/24) and VLAN 20 (10.1.20.0/24) connect to the same Layer 2 switch but cannot communicate with each other. What is required to fix this?
text.hi: VLAN 10 (10.1.10.0/24) aur VLAN 20 (10.1.20.0/24) ke hosts same Layer 2 switch se connected hain lekin ek doosre se communicate nahi kar pa rahe. Ise fix karne ke liye kya zaroori hai?

explanation.en: Each VLAN is a separate broadcast domain with its own IP subnet. A Layer 2 switch never forwards frames between VLANs, so traffic must be routed by a Layer 3 device — a router (router-on-a-stick) or a multilayer switch with SVIs.
explanation.hi: Har VLAN ek alag broadcast domain hai jiska apna IP subnet hai. Layer 2 switch kabhi VLANs ke beech frames forward nahi karta, isliye traffic ko Layer 3 device se route karna padta hai — router (router-on-a-stick) ya SVIs wala multilayer switch.

options.en: A router or Layer 3 switch to route between the two VLANs
options.hi: Dono VLANs ke beech route karne ke liye ek router ya Layer 3 switch

options.en: A second trunk link between the access switches
options.hi: Access switches ke beech ek doosra trunk link

options.en: VTP to synchronize the VLAN database
options.hi: VLAN database synchronize karne ke liye VTP

options.en: PortFast on the host-facing ports
options.hi: Host-facing ports par PortFast

whyWrong.en: More Layer 2 links do not cross the VLAN boundary — routing does.
whyWrong.hi: Zyada Layer 2 links VLAN boundary cross nahi karte — routing karti hai.

whyWrong.en: VTP only distributes VLAN definitions; it does not move traffic between VLANs.
whyWrong.hi: VTP sirf VLAN definitions distribute karta hai; yeh VLANs ke beech traffic move nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: PortFast just speeds up STP convergence on edge ports; it has nothing to do with routing.
whyWrong.hi: PortFast sirf edge ports par STP convergence fast karta hai; iska routing se koi lena dena nahi.

text.en: Which command sequence correctly configures a router-on-a-stick subinterface for VLAN 10?
text.hi: Kaunsa command sequence VLAN 10 ke liye router-on-a-stick subinterface ko sahi configure karta hai?

explanation.en: Router-on-a-stick uses one subinterface per VLAN. The encapsulation dot1q 10 command must come BEFORE the ip address, because IOS refuses an IP on a LAN subinterface until it is tied to a VLAN tag. The subinterface number (.10) is cosmetic, but matching it to the VLAN ID is best practice.
explanation.hi: Router-on-a-stick har VLAN ke liye ek subinterface use karta hai. encapsulation dot1q 10 command ip address se PEHLE aana chahiye, kyunki IOS LAN subinterface par tab tak IP accept nahi karta jab tak woh kisi VLAN tag se na juda ho. Subinterface number (.10) sirf cosmetic hai, lekin ise VLAN ID se match karna best practice hai.

options.en: interface g0/0.10 ; encapsulation dot1q 10 ; ip address 10.1.10.1 255.255.255.0
options.hi: interface g0/0.10 ; encapsulation dot1q 10 ; ip address 10.1.10.1 255.255.255.0

options.en: interface g0/0 ; encapsulation dot1q 10 ; ip address 10.1.10.1 255.255.255.0
options.hi: interface g0/0 ; encapsulation dot1q 10 ; ip address 10.1.10.1 255.255.255.0

options.en: interface g0/0.10 ; ip address 10.1.10.1 255.255.255.0 ; encapsulation dot1q 10
options.hi: interface g0/0.10 ; ip address 10.1.10.1 255.255.255.0 ; encapsulation dot1q 10

options.en: interface g0/0.10 ; switchport access vlan 10 ; ip address 10.1.10.1 255.255.255.0
options.hi: interface g0/0.10 ; switchport access vlan 10 ; ip address 10.1.10.1 255.255.255.0

whyWrong.en: encapsulation dot1q belongs on the subinterface, not on the physical routed interface.
whyWrong.hi: encapsulation dot1q subinterface par lagta hai, physical routed interface par nahi.

whyWrong.en: IOS rejects the IP address if the subinterface has no encapsulation yet — order matters.
whyWrong.hi: Agar subinterface par abhi encapsulation nahi hai toh IOS IP address reject kar deta hai — order matter karta hai.

whyWrong.en: switchport commands exist on switches; router interfaces have no switchport command.
whyWrong.hi: switchport commands switches par hote hain; router interfaces par koi switchport command nahi hota.

text.en: On a Layer 3 switch, interface Vlan20 is in the up/down state. VLAN 20 exists in the VLAN database and the SVI is not shut down. What is the most likely reason?
text.hi: Ek Layer 3 switch par interface Vlan20 up/down state mein hai. VLAN 20 VLAN database mein exist karta hai aur SVI shut down nahi hai. Sabse likely reason kya hai?

explanation.en: SVI autostate: interface VlanX only comes up when the VLAN exists AND at least one Layer 2 port carrying that VLAN (access port in the VLAN, or a trunk allowing it) is up and in STP forwarding. With no live port in VLAN 20, the SVI stays up/down.
explanation.hi: SVI autostate: interface VlanX sirf tab up hota hai jab VLAN exist kare AUR us VLAN ko carry karne wala kam se kam ek Layer 2 port (VLAN mein access port, ya use allow karne wala trunk) up ho aur STP forwarding mein ho. VLAN 20 mein koi live port na hone par SVI up/down hi rehta hai.

options.en: No currently-up access port or trunk is carrying VLAN 20, so autostate keeps the SVI down
options.hi: Abhi koi up access port ya trunk VLAN 20 carry nahi kar raha, isliye autostate SVI ko down rakhta hai

options.en: The SVI is missing the no switchport command
options.hi: SVI par no switchport command missing hai

options.en: ip routing has not been enabled globally
options.hi: ip routing globally enable nahi kiya gaya

options.en: The VLAN must be given a name before its SVI can come up
options.hi: SVI up hone se pehle VLAN ko naam dena zaroori hai

whyWrong.en: no switchport converts a physical port to a routed port; it does not apply to SVIs.
whyWrong.hi: no switchport physical port ko routed port mein badalta hai; yeh SVIs par apply nahi hota.

whyWrong.en: Without ip routing the switch would not route between SVIs, but the SVI could still be up/up.
whyWrong.hi: ip routing ke bina switch SVIs ke beech route nahi karega, lekin SVI phir bhi up/up ho sakta hai.

whyWrong.en: VLAN names are cosmetic and have no effect on SVI state.
whyWrong.hi: VLAN names sirf cosmetic hain aur SVI state par inka koi asar nahi.

text.en: A Layer 3 switch has SVIs Vlan10 (10.1.10.1/24) and Vlan20 (10.1.20.1/24), both up/up. Hosts have correct addresses and gateways, and each host can ping its own gateway SVI — but hosts in VLAN 10 cannot reach hosts in VLAN 20. What is the most likely cause?
text.hi: Ek Layer 3 switch par SVIs Vlan10 (10.1.10.1/24) aur Vlan20 (10.1.20.1/24) hain, dono up/up. Hosts ke addresses aur gateways sahi hain, aur har host apne gateway SVI ko ping kar sakta hai — lekin VLAN 10 ke hosts VLAN 20 ke hosts tak nahi pahunch pa rahe. Sabse likely cause kya hai?

explanation.en: Many Catalyst switches ship with IP routing disabled. Hosts can still ping their local SVI (the switch answers directly), but transit routing between subnets requires the global command ip routing. Enabling it lets the switch route between its connected SVIs immediately.
explanation.hi: Kai Catalyst switches IP routing disabled ke saath aate hain. Hosts phir bhi apne local SVI ko ping kar sakte hain (switch seedha jawab deta hai), lekin subnets ke beech transit routing ke liye global command ip routing chahiye. Ise enable karte hi switch apne connected SVIs ke beech route karne lagta hai.

options.en: ip routing is not enabled globally, so the switch will not route between its SVIs
options.hi: ip routing globally enable nahi hai, isliye switch apne SVIs ke beech route nahi karega

options.en: The two SVIs must share the same subnet to exchange traffic
options.hi: Traffic exchange karne ke liye dono SVIs ka same subnet hona zaroori hai

options.en: Each host needs a static route to the other VLAN
options.hi: Har host ko doosre VLAN ke liye static route chahiye

options.en: An external router is always required to route between SVIs
options.hi: SVIs ke beech route karne ke liye hamesha ek external router chahiye

whyWrong.en: Each VLAN must be a DIFFERENT subnet; overlapping subnets would break routing entirely.
whyWrong.hi: Har VLAN ka ALAG subnet hona chahiye; overlapping subnets routing ko poori tarah tod denge.

whyWrong.en: Hosts only need their default gateway; the switch handles the inter-VLAN path.
whyWrong.hi: Hosts ko sirf apna default gateway chahiye; inter-VLAN path switch handle karta hai.

whyWrong.en: A multilayer switch routes between SVIs on its own — that is the whole point of SVIs.
whyWrong.hi: Multilayer switch SVIs ke beech khud route karta hai — SVIs ka poora point yahi hai.

text.en: Which three elements are required for router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing to work? (Choose three.)
text.hi: Router-on-a-stick inter-VLAN routing kaam karne ke liye kaunse teen elements zaroori hain? (Teen chuno.)

explanation.en: Router-on-a-stick needs: a trunk from switch to router so all VLANs arrive tagged, a subinterface per VLAN whose dot1q tag matches the VLAN ID, and hosts pointing at the right subinterface address as their gateway. The VLAN subnets are directly connected, so no routing protocol is needed.
explanation.hi: Router-on-a-stick ko chahiye: switch se router tak ek trunk taaki saare VLANs tagged pahunchein, har VLAN ke liye ek subinterface jiska dot1q tag VLAN ID se match kare, aur hosts jo sahi subinterface address ko apna gateway banayein. VLAN subnets directly connected hain, isliye koi routing protocol nahi chahiye.

options.en: The switch port facing the router configured as an 802.1Q trunk
options.hi: Router ki taraf wala switch port 802.1Q trunk ki tarah configured ho

options.en: One router subinterface per VLAN with a matching encapsulation dot1q VLAN ID
options.hi: Har VLAN ke liye ek router subinterface jiska encapsulation dot1q VLAN ID match kare

options.en: Hosts using their VLAN's subinterface IP address as their default gateway
options.hi: Hosts apne VLAN ke subinterface IP address ko default gateway ki tarah use karein

options.en: A dynamic routing protocol such as OSPF running between router and switch
options.hi: Router aur switch ke beech OSPF jaisa dynamic routing protocol chal raha ho

options.en: The same IP subnet configured on every subinterface
options.hi: Har subinterface par same IP subnet configured ho

whyWrong.en: The subinterface networks are directly connected routes; OSPF adds nothing for local inter-VLAN routing.
whyWrong.hi: Subinterface networks directly connected routes hain; local inter-VLAN routing mein OSPF kuch add nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: Every VLAN must be a distinct subnet — duplicate subnets on subinterfaces are rejected.
whyWrong.hi: Har VLAN ka alag subnet hona chahiye — subinterfaces par duplicate subnets reject ho jaate hain.

text.en: A network mixes Cisco switches with switches from another vendor. Which discovery protocol can identify directly connected neighbors on both?
text.hi: Ek network mein Cisco switches ke saath doosre vendor ke switches bhi hain. Kaunsa discovery protocol dono par directly connected neighbors identify kar sakta hai?

explanation.en: LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB) is the standards-based discovery protocol supported across vendors. CDP is Cisco proprietary, so third-party switches generally do not speak it.
explanation.hi: LLDP (IEEE 802.1AB) standards-based discovery protocol hai jo saare vendors support karte hain. CDP Cisco proprietary hai, isliye third-party switches aam taur par ise nahi bolte.

options.en: CDP
options.hi: CDP

options.en: LLDP
options.hi: LLDP

options.en: DTP
options.hi: DTP

options.en: VTP
options.hi: VTP

whyWrong.en: CDP is Cisco proprietary and typically unsupported on other vendors' gear.
whyWrong.hi: CDP Cisco proprietary hai aur doosre vendors ke equipment par aam taur par supported nahi hota.

whyWrong.en: DTP negotiates trunking on Cisco switches; it is not a discovery protocol.
whyWrong.hi: DTP Cisco switches par trunking negotiate karta hai; yeh discovery protocol nahi hai.

whyWrong.en: VTP distributes VLAN definitions; it does not discover neighbors.
whyWrong.hi: VTP VLAN definitions distribute karta hai; yeh neighbors discover nahi karta.

text.en: By default, how often does a Cisco device send CDP advertisements, and what is the CDP holdtime?
text.hi: Default mein Cisco device kitni der mein CDP advertisements bhejta hai, aur CDP holdtime kya hai?

explanation.en: CDP defaults: advertisements every 60 seconds, and entries are aged out if nothing is heard for the 180-second holdtime. Remember the contrast with LLDP defaults: 30-second advertisements and 120-second holdtime.
explanation.hi: CDP defaults: har 60 seconds mein advertisements, aur 180-second holdtime tak kuch sunai na de toh entries age out ho jaati hain. LLDP defaults se contrast yaad rakho: 30-second advertisements aur 120-second holdtime.

options.en: Every 60 seconds, holdtime 180 seconds
options.hi: Har 60 seconds, holdtime 180 seconds

options.en: Every 30 seconds, holdtime 120 seconds
options.hi: Har 30 seconds, holdtime 120 seconds

options.en: Every 10 seconds, holdtime 60 seconds
options.hi: Har 10 seconds, holdtime 60 seconds

options.en: Every 5 seconds, holdtime 15 seconds
options.hi: Har 5 seconds, holdtime 15 seconds

whyWrong.en: 30/120 are the default LLDP timers — a favorite exam mix-up.
whyWrong.hi: 30/120 default LLDP timers hain — exam ka favourite mix-up.

whyWrong.en: 10/60 matches neither protocol's defaults.
whyWrong.hi: 10/60 kisi bhi protocol ke defaults se match nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: 5/15 resembles aggressive routing-protocol timers, not CDP.
whyWrong.hi: 5/15 aggressive routing-protocol timers jaisa lagta hai, CDP nahi.

text.en:
Examine this output taken on SW1:

SW1# show cdp neighbors
Capability Codes: R - Router, S - Switch, I - IGMP
Device ID        Local Intrfce     Holdtme    Capability  Platform  Port ID
SW2              Gig 0/1           155        S I         WS-C2960  Gig 0/2
R1               Fas 0/24          142        R           ISR4321   Gig 0/0/1

Which statement about the physical connections is accurate?
text.hi:
SW1 par liya gaya yeh output dekho:

SW1# show cdp neighbors
Capability Codes: R - Router, S - Switch, I - IGMP
Device ID        Local Intrfce     Holdtme    Capability  Platform  Port ID
SW2              Gig 0/1           155        S I         WS-C2960  Gig 0/2
R1               Fas 0/24          142        R           ISR4321   Gig 0/0/1

Physical connections ke baare mein kaunsa statement sahi hai?

explanation.en: In show cdp neighbors, 'Local Intrfce' is the port on the device where you ran the command (SW1), and 'Port ID' is the NEIGHBOR's port. So SW1 Gig0/1 connects to SW2 Gig0/2, and SW1 Fas0/24 connects to R1 Gig0/0/1. Reading these two columns backwards is the classic mistake.
explanation.hi: show cdp neighbors mein 'Local Intrfce' us device ka port hai jahan tumne command chalaya (SW1), aur 'Port ID' NEIGHBOR ka port hai. Isliye SW1 Gig0/1 SW2 Gig0/2 se connect hai, aur SW1 Fas0/24 R1 Gig0/0/1 se. In do columns ko ulta padhna classic mistake hai.

options.en: SW1's Gig 0/1 connects to SW2's Gig 0/2
options.hi: SW1 ka Gig 0/1 SW2 ke Gig 0/2 se connect hai

options.en: SW1's Gig 0/2 connects to SW2's Gig 0/1
options.hi: SW1 ka Gig 0/2 SW2 ke Gig 0/1 se connect hai

options.en: R1's Fas 0/24 connects to SW1's Gig 0/0/1
options.hi: R1 ka Fas 0/24 SW1 ke Gig 0/0/1 se connect hai

options.en: SW2 reaches SW1 through SW2's interface Gig 0/1
options.hi: SW2, SW2 ke interface Gig 0/1 se SW1 tak pahunchta hai

whyWrong.en: This reverses the columns — Local Intrfce belongs to SW1, Port ID belongs to the neighbor.
whyWrong.hi: Yeh columns ko ulta kar deta hai — Local Intrfce SW1 ka hai, Port ID neighbor ka.

whyWrong.en: Fas 0/24 is SW1's local port and Gig 0/0/1 belongs to R1, not SW1.
whyWrong.hi: Fas 0/24 SW1 ka local port hai aur Gig 0/0/1 R1 ka hai, SW1 ka nahi.

whyWrong.en: The output shows SW2 uses Gig 0/2 (the Port ID column) to reach SW1.
whyWrong.hi: Output dikhata hai ki SW2 SW1 tak pahunchne ke liye Gig 0/2 (Port ID column) use karta hai.

text.en: Which three statements about LLDP on Cisco IOS devices are true? (Choose three.)
text.hi: Cisco IOS devices par LLDP ke baare mein kaunse teen statements sahi hain? (Teen chuno.)

explanation.en: Cisco gear ships with CDP on and LLDP off; lldp run turns LLDP on globally. Per interface you can control each direction separately with lldp transmit and lldp receive. LLDP's default timers are 30 s / 120 s (not CDP's 60/180), and LLDP is the IEEE 802.1AB standard, not Cisco proprietary.
explanation.hi: Cisco gear CDP on aur LLDP off ke saath aata hai; lldp run LLDP ko globally on karta hai. Har interface par tum lldp transmit aur lldp receive se dono directions alag-alag control kar sakte ho. LLDP ke default timers 30 s / 120 s hain (CDP ke 60/180 nahi), aur LLDP IEEE 802.1AB standard hai, Cisco proprietary nahi.

options.en: LLDP is disabled by default on most Cisco IOS devices
options.hi: Zyaadatar Cisco IOS devices par LLDP default mein disabled hota hai

options.en: The global command lldp run enables LLDP on the device
options.hi: Global command lldp run device par LLDP enable karta hai

options.en: LLDP transmit and receive can be disabled independently on an interface
options.hi: Interface par LLDP transmit aur receive alag-alag disable kiye ja sakte hain

options.en: LLDP uses the same default timers as CDP (60 s advertisements, 180 s holdtime)
options.hi: LLDP CDP wale hi default timers use karta hai (60 s advertisements, 180 s holdtime)

options.en: LLDP is a Cisco-proprietary enhancement of CDP
options.hi: LLDP CDP ka Cisco-proprietary enhancement hai

whyWrong.en: LLDP defaults are 30-second advertisements with a 120-second holdtime.
whyWrong.hi: LLDP defaults 30-second advertisements aur 120-second holdtime hain.

whyWrong.en: LLDP is the vendor-neutral IEEE 802.1AB standard; CDP is the Cisco-proprietary protocol.
whyWrong.hi: LLDP vendor-neutral IEEE 802.1AB standard hai; CDP Cisco-proprietary protocol hai.

text.en: Type the command that shows full details for every CDP neighbor, including the neighbor's IP address, platform, and IOS version.
text.hi: Woh command type karo jo har CDP neighbor ki full details dikhata hai, jismein neighbor ka IP address, platform aur IOS version shaamil ho.

explanation.en: show cdp neighbors detail expands the summary table into a per-neighbor block containing management IP address, software version, platform, native VLAN, and duplex — invaluable for mapping a network without documentation.
explanation.hi: show cdp neighbors detail summary table ko har neighbor ke liye ek block mein expand karta hai jismein management IP address, software version, platform, native VLAN aur duplex hota hai — bina documentation ke network map karne ke liye bahut kaam ka.

text.en: Two switches are connected by four Gigabit links bundled into a single EtherChannel. Compared with leaving them as four independent links, what is the key advantage?
text.hi: Do switches chaar Gigabit links se connected hain jo ek single EtherChannel mein bundled hain. Inhe chaar independent links rehne dene ke comparison mein key advantage kya hai?

explanation.en: Four separate parallel links form a loop, so STP would block three of them. EtherChannel presents the bundle to STP as ONE logical interface, so all members forward simultaneously, adding bandwidth and giving sub-second failover when a member fails.
explanation.hi: Chaar alag parallel links ek loop banate hain, isliye STP unmein se teen ko block kar dega. EtherChannel bundle ko STP ke saamne EK logical interface ki tarah present karta hai, isliye saare members ek saath forward karte hain, bandwidth badhti hai aur kisi member ke fail hone par sub-second failover milta hai.

options.en: STP treats the bundle as one logical link, so all four physical links forward instead of most being blocked
options.hi: STP bundle ko ek logical link maanta hai, isliye zyaadatar links block hone ki jagah chaaron physical links forward karte hain

options.en: Each physical link runs its own STP instance for faster convergence
options.hi: Har physical link faster convergence ke liye apna STP instance chalata hai

options.en: A single large frame is striped across all four links at once
options.hi: Ek single bada frame ek saath chaaron links par stripe hota hai

options.en: The bundle encrypts traffic between the switches
options.hi: Bundle switches ke beech traffic encrypt karta hai

whyWrong.en: STP runs on the single logical port-channel, not per member — that is the benefit, not per-link instances.
whyWrong.hi: STP single logical port-channel par chalta hai, har member par nahi — fayda yahi hai, per-link instances nahi.

whyWrong.en: Load balancing is per flow (hash of MAC/IP/port); any single frame travels over exactly one member link.
whyWrong.hi: Load balancing per flow hoti hai (MAC/IP/port ka hash); koi bhi single frame exactly ek member link par travel karta hai.

whyWrong.en: EtherChannel provides aggregation and redundancy, not encryption.
whyWrong.hi: EtherChannel aggregation aur redundancy deta hai, encryption nahi.

text.en: SW1's Gi0/1-2 are configured with channel-group 1 mode passive. SW2's matching ports are also set to mode passive. What is the result?
text.hi: SW1 ke Gi0/1-2 channel-group 1 mode passive ke saath configured hain. SW2 ke matching ports bhi mode passive par set hain. Result kya hoga?

explanation.en: LACP passive mode listens but never starts the negotiation. With passive on both ends, no LACP PDUs are initiated and the bundle never forms. At least one side must be active (active/active and active/passive both work).
explanation.hi: LACP passive mode sunta hai lekin kabhi negotiation shuru nahi karta. Dono ends passive hone par koi LACP PDUs initiate nahi hote aur bundle kabhi nahi banta. Kam se kam ek side active honi chahiye (active/active aur active/passive dono kaam karte hain).

options.en: An LACP channel forms because both ends run LACP
options.hi: LACP channel ban jaata hai kyunki dono ends LACP chala rahe hain

options.en: No channel forms because neither side initiates the LACP negotiation
options.hi: Koi channel nahi banta kyunki koi bhi side LACP negotiation initiate nahi karti

options.en: The switches fall back to PAgP and the channel forms
options.hi: Switches PAgP par fall back karte hain aur channel ban jaata hai

options.en: The ports are placed in err-disabled state
options.hi: Ports err-disabled state mein chale jaate hain

whyWrong.en: Merely running LACP is not enough — someone must send the first LACP PDUs, and passive mode never does.
whyWrong.hi: Sirf LACP chalana kaafi nahi — kisi ko pehle LACP PDUs bhejne padte hain, aur passive mode kabhi nahi bhejta.

whyWrong.en: PAgP and LACP are separate protocols; there is no automatic fallback between them.
whyWrong.hi: PAgP aur LACP alag protocols hain; inke beech koi automatic fallback nahi hota.

whyWrong.en: The ports keep working as individual links; a failed negotiation does not err-disable them.
whyWrong.hi: Ports individual links ki tarah kaam karte rehte hain; failed negotiation unhe err-disable nahi karti.

text.en:
Examine this output:

SW1# show etherchannel summary
Flags:  D - down        P - bundled in port-channel
        I - stand-alone s - suspended
        R - Layer3      S - Layer2
        U - in use      f - failed to allocate aggregator

Group  Port-channel  Protocol    Ports
------+-------------+-----------+---------------------------
1      Po1(SU)         LACP      Gi0/1(s)    Gi0/2(P)

What is the most likely reason Gi0/1 shows the s flag?
text.hi:
Yeh output dekho:

SW1# show etherchannel summary
Flags:  D - down        P - bundled in port-channel
        I - stand-alone s - suspended
        R - Layer3      S - Layer2
        U - in use      f - failed to allocate aggregator

Group  Port-channel  Protocol    Ports
------+-------------+-----------+---------------------------
1      Po1(SU)         LACP      Gi0/1(s)    Gi0/2(P)

Gi0/1 par s flag dikhne ka sabse likely reason kya hai?

explanation.en: The s (suspended) flag means the port was excluded from the bundle, most often because a parameter mismatch was detected — speed, duplex, access VLAN, trunk mode/allowed list, or native VLAN differ from the channel. All member ports must have identical Layer 2 configuration.
explanation.hi: s (suspended) flag ka matlab hai port ko bundle se bahar rakha gaya, aksar isliye kyunki parameter mismatch detect hua — speed, duplex, access VLAN, trunk mode/allowed list, ya native VLAN channel se alag hai. Saare member ports ki Layer 2 configuration identical honi chahiye.

options.en: Its configuration (such as speed, duplex, or VLAN settings) does not match the other member or the port-channel
options.hi: Iski configuration (jaise speed, duplex ya VLAN settings) doosre member ya port-channel se match nahi karti

options.en: The cable on Gi0/1 is unplugged
options.hi: Gi0/1 ka cable unplugged hai

options.en: LACP is not running on the port-channel
options.hi: Port-channel par LACP nahi chal raha

options.en: Gi0/1 was administratively shut down
options.hi: Gi0/1 ko administratively shut down kiya gaya

whyWrong.en: An unplugged or dead link shows the D (down) flag, not s.
whyWrong.hi: Unplugged ya dead link D (down) flag dikhata hai, s nahi.

whyWrong.en: The Protocol column shows LACP is in use on group 1.
whyWrong.hi: Protocol column dikhata hai ki group 1 par LACP use ho raha hai.

whyWrong.en: A shutdown interface also shows as down (D), not suspended.
whyWrong.hi: Shutdown interface bhi down (D) dikhta hai, suspended nahi.

text.en: Match each EtherChannel mode combination (one side + other side) to its outcome.
text.hi: Har EtherChannel mode combination (ek side + doosri side) ko uske outcome se match karo.

explanation.en: LACP: active initiates, passive only responds — at least one active is required. PAgP: desirable initiates, auto only responds — at least one desirable is required. Mode on skips negotiation entirely, so it only works when BOTH sides are on; mixing on with a negotiating mode leaves the bundle down.
explanation.hi: LACP: active initiate karta hai, passive sirf respond karta hai — kam se kam ek active zaroori hai. PAgP: desirable initiate karta hai, auto sirf respond karta hai — kam se kam ek desirable zaroori hai. Mode on negotiation poori tarah skip karta hai, isliye yeh sirf tab kaam karta hai jab DONO sides on hon; on ko negotiating mode ke saath milane se bundle down rehta hai.

right.en: LACP negotiates and the channel forms
right.hi: LACP negotiate karta hai aur channel ban jaata hai

right.en: No channel — neither side starts LACP
right.hi: Koi channel nahi — koi bhi side LACP shuru nahi karti

right.en: PAgP negotiates and the channel forms
right.hi: PAgP negotiate karta hai aur channel ban jaata hai

right.en: No channel — on mode never negotiates
right.hi: Koi channel nahi — on mode kabhi negotiate nahi karta

right.en: Channel forms with no negotiation protocol
right.hi: Bina kisi negotiation protocol ke channel ban jaata hai

text.en: Type the command that displays each EtherChannel group, its status flags, protocol, and member ports on one screen.
text.hi: Woh command type karo jo har EtherChannel group, uske status flags, protocol aur member ports ek hi screen par dikhata hai.

explanation.en: show etherchannel summary is the go-to verification command: SU beside the Po interface means Layer 2 and in use, and each member should show P (bundled). Flags such as s (suspended), I (stand-alone), or D (down) point directly at the problem.
explanation.hi: show etherchannel summary go-to verification command hai: Po interface ke saath SU ka matlab hai Layer 2 aur in use, aur har member P (bundled) dikhana chahiye. s (suspended), I (stand-alone) ya D (down) jaise flags seedha problem ki taraf ishara karte hain.

text.en: show interfaces status lists port Gi0/5 in the err-disabled state. Which statement is true?
text.hi: show interfaces status port Gi0/5 ko err-disabled state mein list karta hai. Kaunsa statement sahi hai?

explanation.en: err-disabled means the switch itself disabled the port after a violation — port security, BPDU guard, and similar features trigger it. Fix the root cause first, then bounce the port with shutdown / no shutdown (or configure errdisable recovery for automatic re-enable).
explanation.hi: err-disabled ka matlab hai switch ne khud kisi violation ke baad port disable kiya — port security, BPDU guard aur aise features ise trigger karte hain. Pehle root cause fix karo, phir shutdown / no shutdown se port bounce karo (ya automatic re-enable ke liye errdisable recovery configure karo).

options.en: A protection feature such as port security or BPDU guard shut the port; after fixing the cause, shutdown then no shutdown restores it
options.hi: Port security ya BPDU guard jaise protection feature ne port band kiya; cause fix karne ke baad shutdown phir no shutdown se yeh wapas aa jaata hai

options.en: The port was manually disabled with the shutdown command
options.hi: Port ko shutdown command se manually disable kiya gaya

options.en: The cable is simply disconnected
options.hi: Cable bas disconnected hai

options.en: Autonegotiation failed and the port will recover by itself
options.hi: Autonegotiation fail hua aur port apne aap recover ho jaayega

whyWrong.en: A manual shutdown shows as 'disabled', not 'err-disabled'.
whyWrong.hi: Manual shutdown 'disabled' dikhta hai, 'err-disabled' nahi.

whyWrong.en: An unplugged cable shows 'notconnect'.
whyWrong.hi: Unplugged cable 'notconnect' dikhata hai.

whyWrong.en: err-disabled ports stay down until manually bounced unless errdisable recovery has been configured.
whyWrong.hi: err-disabled ports tab tak down rehte hain jab tak manually bounce na kiye jaayein, jab tak errdisable recovery configure na ho.

text.en:
Users report that file transfers through Fa0/3 are extremely slow, though the link stays up. The neighbor device is hard-coded to full-duplex.

SW1# show interfaces fa0/3 | include duplex|collision|CRC
  Half-duplex, 100Mb/s
  941 input errors, 892 CRC, 45 frame
  3021 collisions, 118 late collisions

What is the diagnosis?
text.hi:
Users report karte hain ki Fa0/3 se file transfers bahut slow hain, jabki link up rehta hai. Neighbor device full-duplex par hard-coded hai.

SW1# show interfaces fa0/3 | include duplex|collision|CRC
  Half-duplex, 100Mb/s
  941 input errors, 892 CRC, 45 frame
  3021 collisions, 118 late collisions

Diagnosis kya hai?

explanation.en: Late collisions plus CRC errors on a half-duplex port whose neighbor is full-duplex is the signature of a duplex mismatch. The full-duplex side transmits whenever it wants; the half-duplex side treats those transmissions as collisions. The link works, but painfully slowly. Set both sides to auto or hard-code both identically.
explanation.hi: Half-duplex port par late collisions plus CRC errors, jabki neighbor full-duplex ho, duplex mismatch ki pehchaan hai. Full-duplex side jab chahe transmit karti hai; half-duplex side un transmissions ko collisions maanti hai. Link kaam karta hai, lekin bahut slow. Dono sides ko auto par set karo ya dono ko identically hard-code karo.

options.en: Duplex mismatch — this side is half-duplex while the neighbor runs full-duplex
options.hi: Duplex mismatch — yeh side half-duplex hai jabki neighbor full-duplex chala raha hai

options.en: A failing cable is bringing the link down repeatedly
options.hi: Kharab cable link ko baar-baar down kar raha hai

options.en: An MTU mismatch is producing giants
options.hi: MTU mismatch giants paida kar raha hai

options.en: STP is intermittently blocking the port
options.hi: STP beech-beech mein port ko block kar raha hai

whyWrong.en: The link is stable and up; a bad cable typically causes flapping or notconnect, not late collisions.
whyWrong.hi: Link stable aur up hai; kharab cable aam taur par flapping ya notconnect karta hai, late collisions nahi.

whyWrong.en: Giants would appear in the giants counter; the symptoms here are collision-related.
whyWrong.hi: Giants giants counter mein dikhte; yahan symptoms collisions se jude hain.

whyWrong.en: A blocked port passes no traffic at all — it would not cause slow transfers with collisions.
whyWrong.hi: Blocked port koi traffic pass hi nahi karta — woh collisions ke saath slow transfers ka cause nahi banega.

text.en:
This message repeats on SW1's console:

%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (10), with SW2 GigabitEthernet0/1 (99).

What is the operational impact, and what is the fix?
text.hi:
SW1 ke console par yeh message baar-baar aa raha hai:

%CDP-4-NATIVE_VLAN_MISMATCH: Native VLAN mismatch discovered on GigabitEthernet0/1 (10), with SW2 GigabitEthernet0/1 (99).

Operational impact kya hai, aur fix kya hai?

explanation.en: The native VLAN is carried untagged, so each switch classifies untagged frames into ITS OWN native VLAN. With 10 on one end and 99 on the other, native-VLAN traffic leaks between VLAN 10 and VLAN 99 — a connectivity and security problem. Make both ends agree, e.g. switchport trunk native vlan 99 on both.
explanation.hi: Native VLAN untagged carry hota hai, isliye har switch untagged frames ko APNE native VLAN mein classify karta hai. Ek end par 10 aur doosre par 99 hone se native-VLAN traffic VLAN 10 aur VLAN 99 ke beech leak hota hai — yeh connectivity aur security dono problem hai. Dono ends ko agree karwao, jaise dono par switchport trunk native vlan 99.

options.en: Untagged frames sent by SW1 in VLAN 10 arrive in VLAN 99 on SW2 (and vice versa); configure the same native VLAN on both trunk ends
options.hi: SW1 dwara VLAN 10 mein bheje gaye untagged frames SW2 par VLAN 99 mein pahunchte hain (aur ulta bhi); dono trunk ends par same native VLAN configure karo

options.en: The trunk stays down until the native VLANs match
options.hi: Native VLANs match hone tak trunk down rehta hai

options.en: CDP automatically shuts down the interface after three warnings
options.hi: Teen warnings ke baad CDP automatically interface shut down kar deta hai

options.en: All tagged VLANs stop crossing the trunk until it is fixed
options.hi: Fix hone tak saare tagged VLANs trunk cross karna band kar dete hain

whyWrong.en: The trunk keeps operating despite the mismatch — that is exactly why the leakage is dangerous.
whyWrong.hi: Mismatch ke bawajood trunk chalta rehta hai — isi wajah se yeh leakage khatarnak hai.

whyWrong.en: CDP only reports the mismatch; it never disables ports.
whyWrong.hi: CDP sirf mismatch report karta hai; yeh kabhi ports disable nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: Tagged VLANs are unaffected; only untagged (native) traffic is misclassified.
whyWrong.hi: Tagged VLANs par koi asar nahi; sirf untagged (native) traffic galat classify hota hai.

text.en:
SW1 and SW2 are joined on Gi0/1 and should trunk, but VLAN traffic is not passing. The same output appears on both switches:

SW1# show interfaces gi0/1 switchport
Name: Gi0/1
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: dynamic auto
Operational Mode: static access
Administrative Trunking Encapsulation: dot1q
Negotiation of Trunking: On

Why did the trunk fail to form?
text.hi:
SW1 aur SW2 Gi0/1 par jude hain aur trunk hona chahiye, lekin VLAN traffic pass nahi ho raha. Dono switches par same output aata hai:

SW1# show interfaces gi0/1 switchport
Name: Gi0/1
Switchport: Enabled
Administrative Mode: dynamic auto
Operational Mode: static access
Administrative Trunking Encapsulation: dot1q
Negotiation of Trunking: On

Trunk kyun nahi bana?

explanation.en: dynamic auto is passive: it will trunk only if the OTHER side asks. With auto on both ends nobody asks, so the operational mode collapses to static access. Fix by setting at least one side to dynamic desirable, or best practice: switchport mode trunk on both (optionally with switchport nonegotiate).
explanation.hi: dynamic auto passive hai: yeh sirf tab trunk karega jab DOOSRI side maange. Dono ends par auto hone se koi nahi maangta, isliye operational mode static access par aa jaata hai. Fix: kam se kam ek side ko dynamic desirable set karo, ya best practice: dono par switchport mode trunk (optionally switchport nonegotiate ke saath).

options.en: Both ends are dynamic auto, so neither initiates DTP and the link falls back to access mode
options.hi: Dono ends dynamic auto hain, isliye koi bhi DTP initiate nahi karta aur link access mode par fall back ho jaata hai

options.en: 802.1Q encapsulation is not supported on these interfaces
options.hi: In interfaces par 802.1Q encapsulation supported nahi hai

options.en: Negotiation of Trunking: On indicates the port is err-disabled
options.hi: Negotiation of Trunking: On batata hai ki port err-disabled hai

options.en: Operational Mode: static access means the interface is shut down
options.hi: Operational Mode: static access ka matlab hai interface shut down hai

whyWrong.en: The output lists dot1q as the administrative encapsulation — it is supported.
whyWrong.hi: Output administrative encapsulation ke roop mein dot1q dikhata hai — yeh supported hai.

whyWrong.en: 'Negotiation of Trunking: On' just means DTP is enabled; err-disabled would appear in the interface status.
whyWrong.hi: 'Negotiation of Trunking: On' ka bas matlab hai DTP enabled hai; err-disabled interface status mein dikhta.

whyWrong.en: Operational mode describes Layer 2 behavior; a shut interface would show 'down' in show interfaces.
whyWrong.hi: Operational mode Layer 2 behavior batata hai; shut interface show interfaces mein 'down' dikhata.

text.en: A PC in VLAN 30 cannot reach its default gateway, an SVI on the distribution switch. Which three Layer 2 checks are appropriate first steps? (Choose three.)
text.hi: VLAN 30 ka ek PC apne default gateway tak nahi pahunch pa raha, jo distribution switch par ek SVI hai. Kaunse teen Layer 2 checks sahi pehle steps hain? (Teen chuno.)

explanation.en: Troubleshoot bottom-up: confirm the physical port state, confirm the correct access VLAN, then confirm the VLAN actually rides the trunk toward the SVI (allowed list, pruning, STP forwarding). Only after Layer 2 is proven should you look at Layer 3.
explanation.hi: Bottom-up troubleshoot karo: pehle physical port state confirm karo, phir sahi access VLAN confirm karo, phir confirm karo ki VLAN sach mein SVI ki taraf trunk par ja raha hai (allowed list, pruning, STP forwarding). Layer 2 prove hone ke baad hi Layer 3 dekhna chahiye.

options.en: Verify the access port is up and assigned to VLAN 30
options.hi: Verify karo ki access port up hai aur VLAN 30 ko assigned hai

options.en: Verify VLAN 30 is allowed and forwarding on the uplink trunk
options.hi: Verify karo ki uplink trunk par VLAN 30 allowed hai aur forwarding mein hai

options.en: Verify the port is not err-disabled or administratively down
options.hi: Verify karo ki port err-disabled ya administratively down nahi hai

options.en: Verify the OSPF adjacency between distribution and core
options.hi: Distribution aur core ke beech OSPF adjacency verify karo

options.en: Verify NAT translations on the Internet edge router
options.hi: Internet edge router par NAT translations verify karo

whyWrong.en: Reaching the local gateway does not involve OSPF — that adjacency matters for traffic beyond the gateway.
whyWrong.hi: Local gateway tak pahunchne mein OSPF involved nahi hai — woh adjacency gateway se aage ke traffic ke liye matter karti hai.

whyWrong.en: NAT applies at the Internet edge; a host-to-gateway failure inside one VLAN is purely a LAN issue.
whyWrong.hi: NAT Internet edge par apply hota hai; ek VLAN ke andar host-to-gateway failure poori tarah LAN issue hai.

text.en: What problem does Spanning Tree Protocol solve in a switched network built with redundant links?
text.hi: Redundant links se bane switched network mein Spanning Tree Protocol kaunsi problem solve karta hai?

explanation.en: Ethernet frames carry no TTL, so a Layer 2 loop lets broadcasts circulate and multiply forever (a broadcast storm) while MAC tables flap between ports. STP logically blocks redundant paths, keeping one loop-free tree while the blocked links remain as backups.
explanation.hi: Ethernet frames mein koi TTL nahi hota, isliye Layer 2 loop mein broadcasts hamesha ghoomte aur badhte rehte hain (broadcast storm) jabki MAC tables ports ke beech flap karti hain. STP redundant paths ko logically block karta hai, ek loop-free tree rakhta hai aur blocked links backup ki tarah bane rehte hain.

options.en: Layer 2 loops, which cause broadcast storms and MAC table instability
options.hi: Layer 2 loops, jo broadcast storms aur MAC table instability paida karte hain

options.en: IP routing loops between subnets
options.hi: Subnets ke beech IP routing loops

options.en: Duplex mismatches on trunk ports
options.hi: Trunk ports par duplex mismatches

options.en: Excessive ARP traffic from hosts
options.hi: Hosts se bahut zyada ARP traffic

whyWrong.en: Routing loops are a Layer 3 issue handled by routing protocols and TTL, not STP.
whyWrong.hi: Routing loops Layer 3 issue hain jinhe routing protocols aur TTL handle karte hain, STP nahi.

whyWrong.en: Duplex mismatches are negotiated (or hard-coded) per link; STP does not manage duplex.
whyWrong.hi: Duplex mismatches har link par negotiate (ya hard-code) hote hain; STP duplex manage nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: ARP volume is normal host behavior; STP does not police it — though a loop makes ARP broadcasts storm.
whyWrong.hi: ARP volume normal host behavior hai; STP ise police nahi karta — haalaanki loop ARP broadcasts ka storm bana deta hai.

text.en: How is the STP root bridge elected?
text.hi: STP root bridge kaise elect hota hai?

explanation.en: The bridge ID is the priority (default 32768, plus the VLAN ID with PVST+ extended system ID) followed by the switch MAC address. Lowest wins. Because most networks leave priority at default, the OLDEST switch (lowest MAC) often becomes root unless you set priority deliberately.
explanation.hi: Bridge ID priority (default 32768, PVST+ extended system ID ke saath plus VLAN ID) aur uske baad switch MAC address hota hai. Sabse kam jeet-ta hai. Kyunki zyaadatar networks priority default par chhod dete hain, SABSE PURANA switch (lowest MAC) aksar root ban jaata hai jab tak tum jaan-boojh kar priority set na karo.

options.en: The switch with the lowest bridge ID wins — lowest priority first, and lowest MAC address as the tiebreaker
options.hi: Sabse kam bridge ID wala switch jeet-ta hai — pehle lowest priority, aur tiebreaker lowest MAC address

options.en: The switch with the highest priority value wins
options.hi: Sabse zyada priority value wala switch jeet-ta hai

options.en: The switch with the fastest uplinks wins
options.hi: Sabse fast uplinks wala switch jeet-ta hai

options.en: The first switch powered on remains root permanently
options.hi: Sabse pehle power on hua switch hamesha root rehta hai

whyWrong.en: Lower is better in the election — a higher priority value makes a switch LESS likely to become root.
whyWrong.hi: Election mein kam better hai — zyada priority value switch ke root banne ke chances KAM karti hai.

whyWrong.en: Link speed influences port cost and path selection, not the root election itself.
whyWrong.hi: Link speed port cost aur path selection ko affect karti hai, root election ko nahi.

whyWrong.en: Boot order does not matter; a better (lower) bridge ID appearing later takes over as root.
whyWrong.hi: Boot order matter nahi karta; baad mein aaya better (lower) bridge ID root ban jaata hai.

text.en:
Four switches in VLAN 1 all use the default priority. Their bridge IDs are:

SW1: priority 32769, MAC 000a.1111.1111
SW2: priority 32769, MAC 000a.2222.2222
SW3: priority 32769, MAC 0009.3333.3333
SW4: priority 32769, MAC 000b.4444.4444

Which switch becomes the root bridge?
text.hi:
VLAN 1 ke chaar switches sab default priority use karte hain. Unke bridge IDs hain:

SW1: priority 32769, MAC 000a.1111.1111
SW2: priority 32769, MAC 000a.2222.2222
SW3: priority 32769, MAC 0009.3333.3333
SW4: priority 32769, MAC 000b.4444.4444

Kaunsa switch root bridge banega?

explanation.en: All priorities are tied at 32769 (32768 + VLAN 1), so the lowest MAC address breaks the tie. Comparing the first bytes: 0009 is lower than 000a and 000b, so SW3 wins. To control root placement deliberately, lower the priority, e.g. spanning-tree vlan 1 priority 4096.
explanation.hi: Saari priorities 32769 (32768 + VLAN 1) par tied hain, isliye lowest MAC address tie todta hai. Pehle bytes compare karo: 0009, 000a aur 000b se kam hai, isliye SW3 jeet-ta hai. Root placement jaan-boojh kar control karne ke liye priority kam karo, jaise spanning-tree vlan 1 priority 4096.

options.en: SW1
options.hi: SW1

options.en: SW2
options.hi: SW2

options.en: SW3
options.hi: SW3

options.en: SW4
options.hi: SW4

whyWrong.en: 000a.1111.1111 is higher than SW3's 0009.3333.3333 in the leading bytes.
whyWrong.hi: 000a.1111.1111 leading bytes mein SW3 ke 0009.3333.3333 se zyada hai.

whyWrong.en: 000a.2222.2222 loses to any 0009 address.
whyWrong.hi: 000a.2222.2222 kisi bhi 0009 address se haar jaata hai.

whyWrong.en: 000b is the highest leading value of the four — SW4 is last in line.
whyWrong.hi: 000b chaaron mein sabse zyada leading value hai — SW4 line mein sabse aakhri hai.

text.en: SW3 is not the root. It has two paths to root bridge SW1: FastEthernet0/1 connects directly to SW1, and GigabitEthernet0/1 connects to SW2, which has a Gigabit link to SW1. Using classic 802.1D costs (100 Mb = 19, 1 Gb = 4), which port becomes SW3's root port?
text.hi: SW3 root nahi hai. Iske paas root bridge SW1 tak do paths hain: FastEthernet0/1 seedha SW1 se connect hai, aur GigabitEthernet0/1 SW2 se connect hai, jiska SW1 tak Gigabit link hai. Classic 802.1D costs (100 Mb = 19, 1 Gb = 4) use karke batao, SW3 ka root port kaunsa banega?

explanation.en: The root port is the port with the LOWEST cumulative cost to the root, not the fewest hops. Via SW2: SW2's root cost 4 plus SW3's Gi port cost 4 = 8. Direct FastEthernet: 19. 8 beats 19, so Gi0/1 is the root port; Fa0/1 becomes non-designated/blocking (assuming SW1 holds the designated role on that segment).
explanation.hi: Root port woh port hai jiska root tak cumulative cost SABSE KAM ho, sabse kam hops nahi. SW2 ke through: SW2 ki root cost 4 plus SW3 ke Gi port ki cost 4 = 8. Direct FastEthernet: 19. 8 19 se behtar hai, isliye Gi0/1 root port hai; Fa0/1 non-designated/blocking ban jaata hai (maan kar ki us segment par designated role SW1 ke paas hai).

options.en: Fa0/1, because it is directly connected to the root
options.hi: Fa0/1, kyunki yeh seedha root se connected hai

options.en: Gi0/1, because the total path cost of 4 + 4 = 8 is lower than the direct path cost of 19
options.hi: Gi0/1, kyunki total path cost 4 + 4 = 8 direct path cost 19 se kam hai

options.en: Fa0/1, because FastEthernet has a lower port cost than Gigabit
options.hi: Fa0/1, kyunki FastEthernet ki port cost Gigabit se kam hai

options.en: Both ports forward and load-share traffic toward the root
options.hi: Dono ports root ki taraf forward karte hain aur traffic load-share karte hain

whyWrong.en: Direct connection is irrelevant — only cumulative path cost decides.
whyWrong.hi: Direct connection irrelevant hai — sirf cumulative path cost decide karti hai.

whyWrong.en: Costs are inverse to speed: FastEthernet = 19, Gigabit = 4.
whyWrong.hi: Costs speed ke ulte hote hain: FastEthernet = 19, Gigabit = 4.

whyWrong.en: Classic STP never load-shares; exactly one root port per non-root switch forwards toward the root.
whyWrong.hi: Classic STP kabhi load-share nahi karta; har non-root switch par exactly ek root port root ki taraf forward karta hai.

text.en: Which two statements about STP bridge IDs and timers are accurate? (Choose two.)
text.hi: STP bridge IDs aur timers ke baare mein kaunse do statements sahi hain? (Do chuno.)

explanation.en: The bridge ID is priority + MAC; with PVST+ the extended system ID embeds the VLAN number into the priority field, which is why VLAN 1 displays 32769. Default timers: hello 2 s, forward delay 15 s, max age 20 s. The LOWEST bridge ID wins the root election.
explanation.hi: Bridge ID priority + MAC hai; PVST+ mein extended system ID VLAN number ko priority field mein embed karta hai, isi wajah se VLAN 1 32769 dikhata hai. Default timers: hello 2 s, forward delay 15 s, max age 20 s. Root election SABSE KAM bridge ID jeet-ta hai.

options.en: The default bridge priority is 32768
options.hi: Default bridge priority 32768 hai

options.en: The bridge ID combines the priority (plus the VLAN ID with PVST+) and the switch MAC address
options.hi: Bridge ID priority (PVST+ ke saath plus VLAN ID) aur switch MAC address ko combine karta hai

options.en: The root bridge is the switch with the highest bridge ID
options.hi: Root bridge woh switch hai jiska bridge ID sabse zyada ho

options.en: Hello BPDUs are sent every 10 seconds by default
options.hi: Hello BPDUs default mein har 10 seconds mein bheje jaate hain

whyWrong.en: Lowest bridge ID wins, not highest.
whyWrong.hi: Sabse kam bridge ID jeet-ta hai, sabse zyada nahi.

whyWrong.en: The default hello time is 2 seconds.
whyWrong.hi: Default hello time 2 seconds hai.

text.en: In which classic 802.1D port state does a switch add source MAC addresses to its table but still refuse to forward user frames?
text.hi: Classic 802.1D ki kis port state mein switch source MAC addresses apni table mein add karta hai lekin user frames forward karne se phir bhi mana karta hai?

explanation.en: The 802.1D progression is blocking, listening, learning, forwarding. Learning is the state where the switch starts populating its MAC table (so it will not have to flood everything the moment it forwards) while still discarding user data frames.
explanation.hi: 802.1D ka sequence hai blocking, listening, learning, forwarding. Learning woh state hai jahan switch apni MAC table bharna shuru karta hai (taaki forward karte hi use sab kuch flood na karna pade) jabki user data frames abhi bhi discard karta hai.

options.en: Blocking
options.hi: Blocking

options.en: Listening
options.hi: Listening

options.en: Learning
options.hi: Learning

options.en: Forwarding
options.hi: Forwarding

whyWrong.en: Blocking ports only receive BPDUs — no MAC learning, no forwarding.
whyWrong.hi: Blocking ports sirf BPDUs receive karte hain — na MAC learning, na forwarding.

whyWrong.en: Listening ports send and receive BPDUs but do not learn MACs yet.
whyWrong.hi: Listening ports BPDUs bhejte aur receive karte hain lekin abhi MACs nahi seekhte.

whyWrong.en: Forwarding ports both learn MACs and forward user traffic.
