whyWrong.hi: Forwarding ports MACs seekhte bhi hain aur user traffic forward bhi karte hain.

text.en: With default 802.1D timers, how long does a port that has just been unblocked take to reach the forwarding state, and why?
text.hi: Default 802.1D timers ke saath, abhi-abhi unblock hue port ko forwarding state tak pahunchne mein kitna time lagta hai, aur kyun?

explanation.en: The forward delay (default 15 s) is applied twice: once for listening and once for learning, giving 30 seconds before user traffic flows. If the switch must first age out old information, max age (20 s) can precede that, making worst-case classic convergence up to 50 seconds — the delay Rapid PVST+ eliminates.
explanation.hi: Forward delay (default 15 s) do baar lagta hai: ek baar listening ke liye aur ek baar learning ke liye, yaani user traffic chalne se pehle 30 seconds. Agar switch ko pehle purani information age out karni pade, toh usse pehle max age (20 s) bhi lag sakta hai, jisse worst-case classic convergence 50 seconds tak ho jaata hai — yahi delay Rapid PVST+ khatam karta hai.

options.en: 30 seconds — 15 seconds in listening plus 15 seconds in learning (one forward delay each)
options.hi: 30 seconds — 15 seconds listening mein plus 15 seconds learning mein (har ek mein ek forward delay)

options.en: 20 seconds — one max age timer
options.hi: 20 seconds — ek max age timer

options.en: 15 seconds — a single forward delay covers both transitional states
options.hi: 15 seconds — ek single forward delay dono transitional states cover karta hai

options.en: 2 seconds — one hello interval
options.hi: 2 seconds — ek hello interval

whyWrong.en: Max age (20 s) is how long stored BPDU info is kept without refresh; it is not the listening/learning time.
whyWrong.hi: Max age (20 s) woh time hai jitni der stored BPDU info bina refresh ke rakhi jaati hai; yeh listening/learning time nahi hai.

whyWrong.en: Forward delay applies per state — 15 seconds each for listening AND learning.
whyWrong.hi: Forward delay har state par lagta hai — listening AUR learning dono ke liye 15-15 seconds.

whyWrong.en: The 2-second hello is the BPDU transmission interval, not a state-transition timer.
whyWrong.hi: 2-second hello BPDU transmission interval hai, state-transition timer nahi.

text.en:
Examine this output:

SW3# show spanning-tree vlan 10
VLAN0010
  Spanning tree enabled protocol ieee
  Root ID    Priority    24586
             Address     0019.e86a.6f80
             Cost        19
             Port        1 (FastEthernet0/1)
             Hello Time   2 sec  Max Age 20 sec  Forward Delay 15 sec

  Bridge ID  Priority    32778  (priority 32768 sys-id-ext 10)
             Address     001b.0c68.2a00

Interface           Role Sts Cost      Prio.Nbr Type
------------------- ---- --- --------- -------- ------
Fa0/1               Root FWD 19        128.1    P2p
Fa0/2               Altn BLK 19        128.2    P2p

Which conclusion is correct?
text.hi:
Yeh output dekho:

SW3# show spanning-tree vlan 10
VLAN0010
  Spanning tree enabled protocol ieee
  Root ID    Priority    24586
             Address     0019.e86a.6f80
             Cost        19
             Port        1 (FastEthernet0/1)
             Hello Time   2 sec  Max Age 20 sec  Forward Delay 15 sec

  Bridge ID  Priority    32778  (priority 32768 sys-id-ext 10)
             Address     001b.0c68.2a00

Interface           Role Sts Cost      Prio.Nbr Type
------------------- ---- --- --------- -------- ------
Fa0/1               Root FWD 19        128.1    P2p
Fa0/2               Altn BLK 19        128.2    P2p

Kaunsa conclusion sahi hai?

explanation.en: The Root ID address (0019.e86a.6f80) differs from SW3's own Bridge ID address (001b.0c68.2a00), so SW3 is not root. The Root ID block names Fa0/1 as the port toward the root at cost 19, matching the Role column (Root, FWD). Fa0/2 is an alternate path held in blocking. When a switch IS the root, the output states 'This bridge is the root'.
explanation.hi: Root ID address (0019.e86a.6f80) SW3 ke apne Bridge ID address (001b.0c68.2a00) se alag hai, isliye SW3 root nahi hai. Root ID block Fa0/1 ko cost 19 par root ki taraf wala port batata hai, jo Role column (Root, FWD) se match karta hai. Fa0/2 ek alternate path hai jo blocking mein rakha gaya hai. Jab koi switch root HOTA hai, toh output mein 'This bridge is the root' likha aata hai.

options.en: SW3 is not the root for VLAN 10; Fa0/1 is its root port with a path cost of 19
options.hi: SW3 VLAN 10 ka root nahi hai; Fa0/1 uska root port hai jiski path cost 19 hai

options.en: SW3 is the root bridge because the output shows a Root ID
options.hi: SW3 root bridge hai kyunki output mein Root ID dikh raha hai

options.en: Fa0/2 is the root port because it is in the blocking state
options.hi: Fa0/2 root port hai kyunki woh blocking state mein hai

options.en: The root bridge is using priority 32778
options.hi: Root bridge priority 32778 use kar raha hai

whyWrong.en: Every switch displays the Root ID it believes in; being root is shown by matching addresses plus the 'This bridge is the root' line.
whyWrong.hi: Har switch woh Root ID dikhata hai jise woh maanta hai; root hona matching addresses plus 'This bridge is the root' line se pata chalta hai.

whyWrong.en: The root port is the FORWARDING port with the best path to root — Fa0/1. Blocked Fa0/2 is the alternate.
whyWrong.hi: Root port woh FORWARDING port hai jiska root tak best path ho — Fa0/1. Blocked Fa0/2 alternate hai.

whyWrong.en: 32778 is SW3's own priority; the root's priority is 24586 (24576 + VLAN 10).
whyWrong.hi: 32778 SW3 ki apni priority hai; root ki priority 24586 (24576 + VLAN 10) hai.

text.en: show spanning-tree vlan 20 on a switch displays Bridge ID priority 32788, yet no spanning-tree priority command has ever been entered. What explains this value?
text.hi: Ek switch par show spanning-tree vlan 20 Bridge ID priority 32788 dikhata hai, jabki kabhi koi spanning-tree priority command enter nahi kiya gaya. Is value ki wajah kya hai?

explanation.en: PVST+ uses the extended system ID: the 12 low-order bits of the priority field carry the VLAN number, so the displayed priority is configured priority + VLAN ID. 32768 + 20 = 32788. This is also why configurable priorities must be multiples of 4096 — only the top 4 bits are settable.
explanation.hi: PVST+ extended system ID use karta hai: priority field ke 12 low-order bits mein VLAN number hota hai, isliye displayed priority = configured priority + VLAN ID. 32768 + 20 = 32788. Isi wajah se configurable priorities 4096 ke multiples hone chahiye — sirf upar ke 4 bits set kiye ja sakte hain.

options.en: The displayed priority is the default 32768 plus the extended system ID, which equals the VLAN number (20)
options.hi: Displayed priority default 32768 plus extended system ID hai, jo VLAN number (20) ke barabar hai

options.en: An administrator previously set the priority to 32788
options.hi: Kisi administrator ne pehle priority 32788 set ki thi

options.en: BPDU guard adds 20 to the priority when it is enabled
options.hi: BPDU guard enable hone par priority mein 20 jod deta hai

options.en: The switch increments the priority by 20 after twenty topology changes
options.hi: Bees topology changes ke baad switch priority 20 se badha deta hai

whyWrong.en: 32788 is not even configurable — priority must be a multiple of 4096 (0, 4096, 8192, ...).
whyWrong.hi: 32788 configure hi nahi ho sakta — priority 4096 ka multiple honi chahiye (0, 4096, 8192, ...).

whyWrong.en: BPDU guard err-disables ports that receive BPDUs; it never modifies the bridge priority.
whyWrong.hi: BPDU guard BPDUs receive karne wale ports ko err-disable karta hai; yeh kabhi bridge priority nahi badalta.

whyWrong.en: Topology change counters are tracked separately and never alter the bridge ID.
whyWrong.hi: Topology change counters alag track hote hain aur kabhi bridge ID nahi badalte.

text.en: Match each classic 802.1D port state to its behavior.
text.hi: Har classic 802.1D port state ko uske behavior se match karo.

explanation.en: The 802.1D sequence is blocking, listening (15 s), learning (15 s), forwarding. RSTP simplifies this to discarding, learning, and forwarding — blocking, listening, and disabled all collapse into discarding.
explanation.hi: 802.1D sequence hai blocking, listening (15 s), learning (15 s), forwarding. RSTP ise simple karke discarding, learning aur forwarding bana deta hai — blocking, listening aur disabled sab discarding mein mil jaate hain.

right.en: Receives BPDUs only; no MAC learning, no forwarding
right.hi: Sirf BPDUs receive karta hai; na MAC learning, na forwarding

right.en: Sends and receives BPDUs but does not learn MACs yet
right.hi: BPDUs bhejta aur receive karta hai lekin abhi MACs nahi seekhta

right.en: Populates the MAC table but still discards user frames
right.hi: MAC table bharta hai lekin user frames abhi bhi discard karta hai

right.en: Forwards user traffic and learns MAC addresses
right.hi: User traffic forward karta hai aur MAC addresses seekhta hai

text.en: What does spanning-tree portfast do when enabled on an access port?
text.hi: Access port par enable karne par spanning-tree portfast kya karta hai?

explanation.en: PortFast lets an edge port begin forwarding immediately, so hosts get link (and DHCP) without the 30-second wait. It belongs ONLY on ports facing end devices — a switch attached to a PortFast port could create a temporary loop, which is why PortFast is normally paired with BPDU guard.
explanation.hi: PortFast edge port ko turant forwarding shuru karne deta hai, taaki hosts ko bina 30-second wait ke link (aur DHCP) mil jaaye. Yeh SIRF end devices ki taraf wale ports par lagna chahiye — PortFast port se juda switch temporary loop bana sakta hai, isi wajah se PortFast ko aam taur par BPDU guard ke saath lagaya jaata hai.

options.en: The port skips the listening and learning states and moves straight to forwarding when it comes up
options.hi: Port up hone par listening aur learning states skip karke seedha forwarding mein chala jaata hai

options.en: The port drops every BPDU it receives
options.hi: Port har receive hua BPDU drop kar deta hai

options.en: The port automatically becomes the designated port for its segment
options.hi: Port automatically apne segment ka designated port ban jaata hai

options.en: The port doubles its BPDU hello rate
options.hi: Port apna BPDU hello rate dugna kar deta hai

whyWrong.en: PortFast still processes BPDUs; ignoring them is BPDU filter's behavior (and it is risky).
whyWrong.hi: PortFast phir bhi BPDUs process karta hai; unhe ignore karna BPDU filter ka behavior hai (aur woh risky hai).

whyWrong.en: Port roles are still decided by normal STP rules; PortFast only accelerates the state transition.
whyWrong.hi: Port roles ab bhi normal STP rules se decide hote hain; PortFast sirf state transition fast karta hai.

whyWrong.en: The hello timer is a bridge-wide setting; PortFast does not change BPDU rates.
whyWrong.hi: Hello timer bridge-wide setting hai; PortFast BPDU rates nahi badalta.

text.en: An access port has PortFast and BPDU guard enabled. A technician plugs a small switch into the port, and that switch sends a BPDU. What happens?
text.hi: Ek access port par PortFast aur BPDU guard enabled hain. Ek technician us port mein chhota switch laga deta hai, aur woh switch ek BPDU bhejta hai. Kya hota hai?

explanation.en: BPDU guard enforces the assumption that an edge port never hears BPDUs. The moment one arrives, the port goes err-disabled, protecting the STP topology from rogue or accidental switches. Recovery requires shutdown / no shutdown (or errdisable recovery).
explanation.hi: BPDU guard is assumption ko enforce karta hai ki edge port par kabhi BPDUs nahi aate. Jaise hi ek aata hai, port err-disabled ho jaata hai, jisse STP topology rogue ya galti se lage switches se bachi rehti hai. Recovery ke liye shutdown / no shutdown (ya errdisable recovery) chahiye.

options.en: The port is placed into the err-disabled state immediately
options.hi: Port turant err-disabled state mein chala jaata hai

options.en: The BPDU is silently ignored and the port stays up
options.hi: BPDU chupchaap ignore ho jaata hai aur port up rehta hai

options.en: The port reverts to a normal STP port and starts the listening state
options.hi: Port normal STP port ban jaata hai aur listening state shuru karta hai

options.en: The two switches negotiate a trunk
options.hi: Dono switches trunk negotiate karte hain

whyWrong.en: Silently ignoring BPDUs describes BPDU filter — a different (and more dangerous) feature.
whyWrong.hi: BPDUs ko chupchaap ignore karna BPDU filter hai — ek alag (aur zyada khatarnak) feature.

whyWrong.en: Reverting to normal STP on receipt of a BPDU is plain PortFast behavior WITHOUT BPDU guard.
whyWrong.hi: BPDU aane par normal STP par wapas jaana BPDU guard ke BINA plain PortFast ka behavior hai.

whyWrong.en: DTP negotiates trunks; BPDU guard acts long before any trunk negotiation matters.
whyWrong.hi: DTP trunks negotiate karta hai; BPDU guard kisi bhi trunk negotiation ke matter karne se bahut pehle act karta hai.

text.en: In RSTP, which port role describes a discarding port that offers an alternate path toward the root bridge and can rapidly take over if the root port fails?
text.hi: RSTP mein kaunsa port role us discarding port ko describe karta hai jo root bridge ki taraf alternate path deta hai aur root port fail hone par turant uski jagah le sakta hai?

explanation.en: The alternate port is RSTP's pre-computed fallback for the root port: it stays discarding but can transition to root port almost instantly. This standby knowledge is a key reason RSTP converges so much faster than 802.1D.
explanation.hi: Alternate port RSTP ka root port ke liye pehle se calculated fallback hai: yeh discarding rehta hai lekin lagbhag turant root port mein transition kar sakta hai. Yeh standby knowledge ek badi wajah hai ki RSTP 802.1D se itna jaldi converge karta hai.

options.en: Alternate
options.hi: Alternate

options.en: Backup
options.hi: Backup

options.en: Designated
options.hi: Designated

options.en: Root
options.hi: Root

whyWrong.en: A backup port backs up a DESIGNATED port on the same shared segment (two ports of one switch on a hub) — a rare case.
whyWrong.hi: Backup port usi shared segment par ek DESIGNATED port ka backup hota hai (hub par ek switch ke do ports) — rare case.

whyWrong.en: Designated ports are forwarding ports — one per segment, closest to the root.
whyWrong.hi: Designated ports forwarding ports hote hain — har segment par ek, root ke sabse paas wala.

whyWrong.en: The root port is the active forwarding path to the root, not the standby.
whyWrong.hi: Root port root tak active forwarding path hai, standby nahi.

text.en: Which three statements about RSTP and Rapid PVST+ are true? (Choose three.)
text.hi: RSTP aur Rapid PVST+ ke baare mein kaunse teen statements sahi hain? (Teen chuno.)

explanation.en: RSTP (802.1w) collapses blocking/listening/disabled into discarding, and Cisco's Rapid PVST+ runs one such instance per VLAN. Fast convergence comes from the proposal/agreement handshake between switches on full-duplex point-to-point links plus pre-computed alternate ports — not from timers.
explanation.hi: RSTP (802.1w) blocking/listening/disabled ko discarding mein mila deta hai, aur Cisco ka Rapid PVST+ har VLAN ke liye ek aisa instance chalata hai. Fast convergence full-duplex point-to-point links par switches ke beech proposal/agreement handshake aur pehle se calculated alternate ports se aata hai — timers se nahi.

options.en: RSTP reduces the port states to discarding, learning, and forwarding
options.hi: RSTP port states ko discarding, learning aur forwarding tak kam kar deta hai

options.en: Rapid PVST+ runs a separate RSTP instance for every VLAN
options.hi: Rapid PVST+ har VLAN ke liye alag RSTP instance chalata hai

options.en: RSTP converges quickly using a proposal/agreement handshake on point-to-point links
options.hi: RSTP point-to-point links par proposal/agreement handshake use karke jaldi converge karta hai

options.en: RSTP requires PortFast on trunk links to converge quickly
options.hi: RSTP ko jaldi converge karne ke liye trunk links par PortFast chahiye

options.en: An RSTP backup port provides an alternate path to the root bridge
options.hi: RSTP backup port root bridge tak alternate path deta hai

whyWrong.en: The edge-port (PortFast) concept applies to host-facing ports; switch-to-switch links converge via the proposal/agreement mechanism.
whyWrong.hi: Edge-port (PortFast) concept host-facing ports par apply hota hai; switch-to-switch links proposal/agreement mechanism se converge hote hain.

whyWrong.en: The path toward the root is the ALTERNATE port's job; a backup port protects a designated port on a shared segment.
whyWrong.hi: Root ki taraf path ALTERNATE port ka kaam hai; backup port shared segment par designated port ko protect karta hai.

text.en: Type the global configuration command that switches the spanning-tree mode to Rapid PVST+.
text.hi: Woh global configuration command type karo jo spanning-tree mode ko Rapid PVST+ par switch karta hai.

explanation.en: spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst converts every VLAN instance to RSTP (802.1w) behavior. It interoperates with legacy 802.1D neighbors by falling back to classic timers on those ports, so it can be deployed gradually.
explanation.hi: spanning-tree mode rapid-pvst har VLAN instance ko RSTP (802.1w) behavior mein convert karta hai. Yeh legacy 802.1D neighbors ke saath un ports par classic timers par fall back karke interoperate karta hai, isliye ise dheere-dheere deploy kiya ja sakta hai.

text.en: Which wireless deployment model uses lightweight access points whose configuration, security policy, and RF management are centralized on a controller?
text.hi: Kaunsa wireless deployment model lightweight access points use karta hai jinki configuration, security policy aur RF management ek controller par centralized hoti hai?

explanation.en: In the split-MAC model, lightweight APs handle real-time 802.11 functions while the WLC centralizes management, authentication, RF tuning, and roaming. Adding or reconfiguring hundreds of APs then happens in one place instead of box by box.
explanation.hi: Split-MAC model mein lightweight APs real-time 802.11 functions handle karte hain jabki WLC management, authentication, RF tuning aur roaming ko centralize karta hai. Isse saikdon APs ko add ya reconfigure karna ek hi jagah se hota hai, har box par alag-alag nahi.

options.en: Split-MAC architecture with a wireless LAN controller (WLC)
options.hi: Wireless LAN controller (WLC) ke saath split-MAC architecture

options.en: Autonomous AP architecture
options.hi: Autonomous AP architecture

options.en: Ad hoc (IBSS) networking
options.hi: Ad hoc (IBSS) networking

options.en: Workgroup bridge deployment
options.hi: Workgroup bridge deployment

whyWrong.en: Autonomous APs are self-contained and individually managed — the opposite of centralized control.
whyWrong.hi: Autonomous APs self-contained hote hain aur alag-alag manage hote hain — centralized control ka ulta.

whyWrong.en: Ad hoc mode is client-to-client with no AP or controller at all.
whyWrong.hi: Ad hoc mode client-to-client hai jismein na AP hota hai na controller.

whyWrong.en: A workgroup bridge connects wired-only devices to a WLAN; it is a client role, not an architecture.
whyWrong.hi: Workgroup bridge wired-only devices ko WLAN se connect karta hai; yeh client role hai, architecture nahi.

text.en: Which protocol and ports does a lightweight AP use to build its control and data tunnels to the WLC?
text.hi: Lightweight AP WLC tak apne control aur data tunnels banane ke liye kaunsa protocol aur ports use karta hai?

explanation.en: CAPWAP builds two UDP tunnels from AP to WLC: control on UDP 5246 (DTLS-encrypted management and configuration) and data on UDP 5247 (client traffic, encryption optional). These ports must be permitted through any firewall between APs and the controller.
explanation.hi: CAPWAP AP se WLC tak do UDP tunnels banata hai: control UDP 5246 par (DTLS-encrypted management aur configuration) aur data UDP 5247 par (client traffic, encryption optional). APs aur controller ke beech kisi bhi firewall par yeh ports permit hone chahiye.

options.en: CAPWAP, using UDP 5246 for control and UDP 5247 for data
options.hi: CAPWAP, control ke liye UDP 5246 aur data ke liye UDP 5247 use karke

options.en: CAPWAP, using TCP 5246 and TCP 5247
options.hi: CAPWAP, TCP 5246 aur TCP 5247 use karke

options.en: GRE, using IP protocol 47
options.hi: GRE, IP protocol 47 use karke

options.en: LWAPP, using UDP 12222 and 12223
options.hi: LWAPP, UDP 12222 aur 12223 use karke

whyWrong.en: CAPWAP runs over UDP, not TCP.
whyWrong.hi: CAPWAP UDP par chalta hai, TCP par nahi.

whyWrong.en: GRE is a generic tunneling protocol; it is not what lightweight APs use to reach a WLC.
whyWrong.hi: GRE ek generic tunneling protocol hai; lightweight APs WLC tak pahunchne ke liye ise use nahi karte.

whyWrong.en: LWAPP (which used 12222/12223) is the legacy predecessor that CAPWAP replaced.
whyWrong.hi: LWAPP (jo 12222/12223 use karta tha) legacy predecessor hai jise CAPWAP ne replace kiya.

text.en: A branch-office AP must keep serving wireless clients and switch their traffic onto the local LAN even when the WAN link to the central WLC goes down. Which AP mode is appropriate?
text.hi: Branch-office AP ko wireless clients serve karte rehna hai aur unka traffic local LAN par switch karte rehna hai, tab bhi jab central WLC tak WAN link down ho jaaye. Kaunsa AP mode sahi hai?

explanation.en: FlexConnect (formerly H-REAP) lets an AP switch client traffic locally at the branch and continue serving existing WLANs while the controller is unreachable. It is the standard design for small sites managed by a central WLC across a WAN.
explanation.hi: FlexConnect (pehle H-REAP) AP ko branch par client traffic locally switch karne deta hai aur controller unreachable hone par bhi existing WLANs serve karte rehne deta hai. WAN ke across central WLC se manage hone wali chhoti sites ke liye yahi standard design hai.

options.en: FlexConnect
options.hi: FlexConnect

options.en: Local
options.hi: Local

options.en: Monitor
options.hi: Monitor

options.en: Sniffer
options.hi: Sniffer

whyWrong.en: Local mode tunnels ALL client traffic to the WLC via CAPWAP — if the WAN fails, client service stops.
whyWrong.hi: Local mode SAARA client traffic CAPWAP se WLC tak tunnel karta hai — WAN fail hone par client service ruk jaati hai.

whyWrong.en: Monitor mode is a dedicated sensor for rogue/IDS scanning and serves no clients.
whyWrong.hi: Monitor mode rogue/IDS scanning ke liye dedicated sensor hai aur koi clients serve nahi karta.

whyWrong.en: Sniffer mode captures 802.11 frames for a protocol analyzer and serves no clients.
whyWrong.hi: Sniffer mode protocol analyzer ke liye 802.11 frames capture karta hai aur koi clients serve nahi karta.

text.en: In the split-MAC architecture, which three functions are handled by the WLC rather than the lightweight AP? (Choose three.)
text.hi: Split-MAC architecture mein kaunse teen functions lightweight AP ki jagah WLC handle karta hai? (Teen chuno.)

explanation.en: The WLC owns non-real-time control functions: association/authentication, RF resource management (RRM), roaming coordination, and security/QoS policy. The AP keeps everything with hard real-time deadlines: beacons, probe responses, per-frame acknowledgments, and per-frame encryption.
explanation.hi: WLC non-real-time control functions sambhalta hai: association/authentication, RF resource management (RRM), roaming coordination, aur security/QoS policy. AP woh sab rakhta hai jinki hard real-time deadlines hain: beacons, probe responses, per-frame acknowledgments aur per-frame encryption.

options.en: Client association and authentication processing
options.hi: Client association aur authentication processing

options.en: Radio resource management, such as channel and power assignment
options.hi: Radio resource management, jaise channel aur power assignment

options.en: Security and QoS policy management
options.hi: Security aur QoS policy management

options.en: Transmitting beacons and probe responses
options.hi: Beacons aur probe responses transmit karna

options.en: Sending real-time acknowledgments for received 802.11 frames
options.hi: Receive hue 802.11 frames ke liye real-time acknowledgments bhejna

whyWrong.en: Beacons and probe responses have strict timing and are generated by the AP itself.
whyWrong.hi: Beacons aur probe responses ki timing strict hoti hai aur inhe AP khud generate karta hai.

whyWrong.en: 802.11 ACKs must be sent within microseconds — only the AP radio can do that.
whyWrong.hi: 802.11 ACKs microseconds ke andar bhejne padte hain — yeh sirf AP radio kar sakta hai.

text.en: Match each lightweight AP mode to its function.
text.hi: Har lightweight AP mode ko uske function se match karo.

explanation.en: Local and FlexConnect serve clients (tunneled vs. locally switched). Monitor, sniffer, and rogue detector are dedicated non-client modes: monitor scans the air, sniffer feeds a packet analyzer such as Wireshark, and rogue detector works from the wired side with its radio disabled. Bridge mode (not listed) provides mesh/point-to-point links.
explanation.hi: Local aur FlexConnect clients serve karte hain (tunneled vs. locally switched). Monitor, sniffer aur rogue detector dedicated non-client modes hain: monitor hawa ko scan karta hai, sniffer Wireshark jaise packet analyzer ko data deta hai, aur rogue detector radio disabled karke wired side se kaam karta hai. Bridge mode (list mein nahi) mesh/point-to-point links deta hai.

right.en: Default mode; serves clients and tunnels their traffic to the WLC
right.hi: Default mode; clients serve karta hai aur unka traffic WLC tak tunnel karta hai

right.en: Can switch client traffic locally if the WLC becomes unreachable
right.hi: WLC unreachable hone par client traffic locally switch kar sakta hai

right.en: Captures 802.11 frames and forwards them to a protocol analyzer
right.hi: 802.11 frames capture karke protocol analyzer ko forward karta hai

right.en: Uses only its wired connection to match wired traffic against known rogue MACs
right.hi: Sirf apna wired connection use karke wired traffic ko known rogue MACs se match karta hai

right.en: Radio-only sensor that scans channels for rogues and IDS events, serving no clients
right.hi: Radio-only sensor jo rogues aur IDS events ke liye channels scan karta hai, koi clients serve nahi karta

text.en: On a wireless LAN controller, which interface type is created to bind a WLAN's client traffic to a specific VLAN?
text.hi: Wireless LAN controller par WLAN ke client traffic ko kisi specific VLAN se bind karne ke liye kaunsa interface type banaya jaata hai?

explanation.en: A dynamic interface on the WLC maps to one VLAN, and each WLAN is tied to a dynamic interface so client traffic lands in the right VLAN and subnet on the wired side. Think of it as the WLC's equivalent of an access VLAN assignment.
explanation.hi: WLC par dynamic interface ek VLAN se map hota hai, aur har WLAN ek dynamic interface se juda hota hai taaki client traffic wired side par sahi VLAN aur subnet mein pahunche. Ise WLC ka access VLAN assignment wala version samjho.

options.en: Dynamic interface
options.hi: Dynamic interface

options.en: Virtual interface
options.hi: Virtual interface

options.en: Service port interface
options.hi: Service port interface

options.en: Redundancy port
options.hi: Redundancy port

whyWrong.en: The virtual interface handles client-facing services like web-auth redirects, not VLAN mapping.
whyWrong.hi: Virtual interface web-auth redirects jaise client-facing services handle karta hai, VLAN mapping nahi.

whyWrong.en: The service port is an out-of-band management port, separate from data traffic.
whyWrong.hi: Service port ek out-of-band management port hai, data traffic se alag.

whyWrong.en: The redundancy port links two WLCs for high availability, not clients to VLANs.
whyWrong.hi: Redundancy port high availability ke liye do WLCs ko jodta hai, clients ko VLANs se nahi.

text.en: Which combination provides secure management access to a wireless LAN controller?
text.hi: Kaunsa combination wireless LAN controller ka secure management access deta hai?

explanation.en: Management sessions should always be encrypted: HTTPS protects GUI logins and SSH protects the CLI. Best practice is to explicitly disable HTTP and Telnet on the WLC and restrict which networks may reach the management interface.
explanation.hi: Management sessions hamesha encrypted hone chahiye: HTTPS GUI logins ko protect karta hai aur SSH CLI ko. Best practice hai WLC par HTTP aur Telnet ko explicitly disable karna aur restrict karna ki kaunse networks management interface tak pahunch sakte hain.

options.en: HTTPS for the web GUI and SSH for the CLI
options.hi: Web GUI ke liye HTTPS aur CLI ke liye SSH

options.en: HTTP for the web GUI and Telnet for the CLI
options.hi: Web GUI ke liye HTTP aur CLI ke liye Telnet

options.en: SNMPv1 with a public read-write community
options.hi: Public read-write community ke saath SNMPv1

options.en: Opening the service port to the guest VLAN
options.hi: Service port ko guest VLAN ke liye khol dena

whyWrong.en: HTTP and Telnet send credentials in cleartext and should be disabled.
whyWrong.hi: HTTP aur Telnet credentials cleartext mein bhejte hain aur inhe disable kar dena chahiye.

whyWrong.en: SNMPv1 has no encryption and community-string-only security; SNMPv3 is the secure option.
whyWrong.hi: SNMPv1 mein koi encryption nahi hai aur security sirf community string par hai; SNMPv3 secure option hai.

whyWrong.en: The service port is for out-of-band maintenance and must never be exposed to user or guest networks.
whyWrong.hi: Service port out-of-band maintenance ke liye hai aur ise kabhi user ya guest networks ke saamne expose nahi karna chahiye.

text.en: A WLC is configured with the address 192.0.2.1 on an interface that is never routed on the network. Which interface is this, and what is it used for?
text.hi: Ek WLC ek aise interface par 192.0.2.1 address ke saath configured hai jo network par kabhi route nahi hota. Yeh kaunsa interface hai, aur kis kaam aata hai?

explanation.en: The virtual interface uses a non-routable placeholder address (commonly 192.0.2.1 or historically 1.1.1.1) that the WLC presents to wireless clients for functions like the web-auth login redirect and as the relay point in client DHCP handling. It must be identical on all WLCs in a mobility group.
explanation.hi: Virtual interface ek non-routable placeholder address use karta hai (aam taur par 192.0.2.1 ya pehle 1.1.1.1) jo WLC wireless clients ko web-auth login redirect jaise functions ke liye aur client DHCP handling mein relay point ki tarah dikhata hai. Mobility group ke saare WLCs par yeh identical hona chahiye.

options.en: The virtual interface — it supports client-facing functions such as web authentication redirects and DHCP relay
options.hi: Virtual interface — yeh web authentication redirects aur DHCP relay jaise client-facing functions support karta hai

options.en: The management interface — it terminates CAPWAP tunnels from the APs
options.hi: Management interface — yeh APs ke CAPWAP tunnels terminate karta hai

options.en: A dynamic interface — it maps a WLAN to a VLAN
options.hi: Dynamic interface — yeh WLAN ko VLAN se map karta hai

options.en: The service port — it provides out-of-band access for maintenance
options.hi: Service port — yeh maintenance ke liye out-of-band access deta hai

whyWrong.en: The management interface uses a real, routable address — APs must reach it to build CAPWAP tunnels.
whyWrong.hi: Management interface real, routable address use karta hai — CAPWAP tunnels banane ke liye APs ko ispar pahunchna padta hai.

whyWrong.en: Dynamic interfaces carry client data onto VLANs and use routable subnet addresses.
whyWrong.hi: Dynamic interfaces client data ko VLANs par le jaate hain aur routable subnet addresses use karte hain.

whyWrong.en: The service port has its own address on a dedicated out-of-band network.
whyWrong.hi: Service port ka ek dedicated out-of-band network par apna address hota hai.

text.en: Which WLC QoS profile should be applied to a WLAN dedicated to voice traffic?
text.hi: Voice traffic ke liye dedicated WLAN par kaunsa WLC QoS profile apply karna chahiye?

explanation.en: The WLC QoS profiles rank Platinum (voice), Gold (video), Silver (best effort — the default), and Bronze (background). Applying Platinum lets voice frames receive priority treatment over the air and appropriate markings toward the wired network.
explanation.hi: WLC QoS profiles ki ranking hai Platinum (voice), Gold (video), Silver (best effort — default), aur Bronze (background). Platinum apply karne se voice frames ko hawa mein priority treatment milta hai aur wired network ki taraf sahi markings milti hain.

options.en: Platinum
options.hi: Platinum

options.en: Gold
options.hi: Gold

options.en: Silver
options.hi: Silver

options.en: Bronze
options.hi: Bronze

whyWrong.en: Gold is intended for video traffic.
whyWrong.hi: Gold video traffic ke liye hai.

whyWrong.en: Silver is the best-effort default — inadequate for latency-sensitive voice.
whyWrong.hi: Silver best-effort default hai — latency-sensitive voice ke liye kaafi nahi.

whyWrong.en: Bronze is background priority, the lowest class, used for things like guest traffic.
whyWrong.hi: Bronze background priority hai, sabse neeche wali class, jo guest traffic jaisi cheezon ke liye use hoti hai.

text.en: Which three steps are part of creating a functional WLAN on a wireless LAN controller? (Choose three.)
text.hi: Wireless LAN controller par functional WLAN banane ke kaunse teen steps hain? (Teen chuno.)

explanation.en: The WLC workflow: build the dynamic interface (VLAN mapping), define the WLAN (profile name, SSID, ID) and bind it to that interface, then set the security policy and enable it — a new WLAN is disabled by default. The WLC then pushes the WLAN to the APs automatically.
explanation.hi: WLC workflow: dynamic interface banao (VLAN mapping), WLAN define karo (profile name, SSID, ID) aur use us interface se bind karo, phir security policy set karke use enable karo — naya WLAN default mein disabled hota hai. Iske baad WLC WLAN ko automatically APs tak push kar deta hai.

options.en: Create or select a dynamic interface tied to the correct VLAN
options.hi: Sahi VLAN se juda dynamic interface banao ya select karo

options.en: Create the WLAN with a profile name, SSID, and ID, and map it to that interface
options.hi: Profile name, SSID aur ID ke saath WLAN banao, aur use us interface se map karo

options.en: Configure the security settings (for example WPA2/WPA3 PSK or 802.1X) and enable the WLAN
options.hi: Security settings configure karo (jaise WPA2/WPA3 PSK ya 802.1X) aur WLAN enable karo

options.en: Manually configure CAPWAP tunnel endpoints on each access point
options.hi: Har access point par CAPWAP tunnel endpoints manually configure karo

options.en: Assign a unique IP address to the SSID itself
options.hi: SSID ko khud ek unique IP address assign karo

whyWrong.en: APs discover and join the WLC automatically (DHCP option 43, DNS, broadcast); CAPWAP tunnels are never configured per WLAN.
whyWrong.hi: APs WLC ko automatically discover aur join karte hain (DHCP option 43, DNS, broadcast); CAPWAP tunnels kabhi per WLAN configure nahi hote.

whyWrong.en: SSIDs are names, not IP endpoints — clients get addresses from the VLAN's subnet via DHCP.
whyWrong.hi: SSIDs naam hain, IP endpoints nahi — clients VLAN ke subnet se DHCP ke through addresses lete hain.
